definition_zh: 艺术的；有艺术性的；有艺术才华的；艺术家的
definition_en: relating to art or artists, or showing the skill and taste associated with art
core_image: 一只手把颜料、线条与留白安排成一个让人愿意多看一会儿的整体
scene: 评审在一幅海报前停住，指出配色与留白都恰到好处。The jury praised the poster for its artistic balance of colour and empty space.
sceneCN: 这里 artistic 指「看得出经过审美安排、具有艺术性」（第 3 个义项：呈现可见的品味与设计感）；句意为评审称赞这张海报在色彩与留白上达到了艺术性的平衡。

pos.zh: 艺术的；艺术家的；有艺术才华的；有艺术性的

collocations.zh: 艺术家气质；艺术家的敏感性情
艺术创作上的自由处理（允许偏离事实）

derivatives.zh: art + -ist（人）→ 艺术家：从「技艺」转到「以艺术为业的人」
artist + -ry（技艺、实践）→ 艺术技巧：从「人」转到「人所具备的手上功夫」
artistic + -ally（副词后缀）→ 在艺术上；从「性质」转到「方式」
art + -y（形容词后缀，口语）→ 冒充艺术品味的；语义偏移为带贬义的「做作」
arty + -ness（名词后缀）→ 艺术腔调；从「做作的」转到「做作的艺术气」

senses.title: Belonging to art as a field
senses.definition: of or connected with art and the people who make it
senses.definitionCN: 与艺术以及从事艺术的人有关的
senses.example: She wrote her thesis on artistic traditions of the northern courts.
senses.exampleCN: 她的论文研究北方宫廷的艺术传统。
senses.why: The suffix -ic simply turns the noun artist into an adjective of relation, so this sense adds no praise: it only says which field is meant.
senses.whyCN: -ic 只是把名词 artist 变成关系形容词，因此这个义项不含褒贬，只说明所说属于哪个领域。

senses.title: Having a gift for making art
senses.definition: able to create art, or to judge it with unusual sensitivity
senses.definitionCN: 有能力创作艺术，或对艺术有格外敏锐的判断力
senses.example: The teachers noticed early that the boy was unusually artistic.
senses.exampleCN: 老师们很早就注意到这个男孩有非同寻常的艺术天赋。
senses.why: The quality named by the adjective can be a permanent capacity of a person, not just a link to a profession; the word moves from the field to the mind that works in it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词所表的性质可以是人的一种长期能力，而不只是与职业的关联；词义因此从「领域」转到「在其中工作的头脑」。

senses.title: Arranged with visible taste
senses.titleCN: 安排得有品味、有艺术性
senses.definition: showing good design and a pleasing visual arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 表现出良好的设计感与悦目的视觉安排
senses.example: The jury praised the poster for its artistic balance of colour and empty space.
senses.exampleCN: 评审称赞这张海报在色彩与留白上达到了艺术性的平衡。
senses.why: Once artistic means 'marked by an artist's judgement', it can describe the result rather than the maker: a layout that looks as if a trained eye arranged it.
senses.whyCN: 当 artistic 表示「带着艺术家的判断」时，它就能描述成品而非制作者：一个看起来像由训练有素的眼睛安排过的版面。

senses.title: Characteristic of one maker's hand
senses.titleCN: 带有某位创作者的个人手法
senses.definition: typical of a particular artist's way of working
senses.definitionCN: 体现出某位艺术家特有的工作方式
senses.example: The attribution rests on an artistic signature of short, broken strokes.
senses.exampleCN: 这一归属判断依据的是短促断续笔触所形成的个人艺术特征。
senses.why: A style is a personal habit made visible, so artistic can point to the fingerprint of one hand inside a work.
senses.whyCN: 风格是个人习惯的可视化，因此 artistic 可以指作品内部属于某只手的「指纹」。

senses.title: Inventive rather than literal
senses.titleCN: 富于想象而非照实记录
senses.definition: using imagination and creative choice rather than copying facts
senses.definitionCN: 运用想象与创造性选择，而不是照搬事实
senses.example: The documentary takes an artistic view of the city rather than a statistical one.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片对这座城市采取艺术化的视角，而非统计式的视角。
senses.why: Art is traditionally opposed to mere recording; when the word describes a choice, it means the imagination has been allowed to shape the material.
senses.whyCN: 艺术传统上与单纯记录相对；当这个词描述一种选择时，意思是允许想象去塑形材料。

senses.title: Licence to depart from fact
senses.titleCN: 为效果而偏离事实的自由
senses.definition: the freedom to change facts for the sake of effect, in the fixed phrase artistic licence
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法 artistic licence 中，指为了效果而改动事实的自由
senses.example: The film takes artistic licence with the dates of the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片对条约的日期作了艺术化的改动。
senses.why: If art is invention, then a maker may depart from the record without breaking the rules of the craft; the phrase names that permitted departure.
senses.whyCN: 如果艺术就是创造，那么创作者就可以偏离记录而不违犯这门手艺的规则；这个固定说法正是指这种被允许的偏离。

senses.title: A refined eye in daily life
senses.titleCN: 日常生活中敏锐的审美眼光
senses.definition: showing sensitive taste in matters outside art
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术之外的日常事物上表现出敏锐的品味
senses.example: Her artistic eye caught the one chair that ruined the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她那双有艺术感觉的眼睛一下就看出那把破坏整体效果的椅子。
senses.why: The trained attention of an artist can be applied to ordinary scenes, so artistic extends from works to the way someone notices the world.
senses.whyCN: 艺术家训练有素的注意力可以用在日常场景中，因此 artistic 从作品延伸到一个人观察世界的方式。

senses.title: The mood credited to artists
senses.titleCN: 人们认为艺术家应有的性情
senses.definition: sensitive, imaginative and sometimes temperamental, as artists are popularly supposed to be
senses.definitionCN: 敏感、富于想象、有时喜怒无常，即大众设想中的艺术家性格
senses.example: He had the artistic temperament without the artistic discipline.
senses.exampleCN: 他有艺术家的性情，却没有艺术家的自律。
senses.why: This sense is a stereotype attached to the profession: the adjective transfers a supposed personality from the group to an individual.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是附着在职业上的刻板印象：形容词把一种被认为属于该群体的性格转到个人身上。

intro.en: Artistic entered English in the eighteenth century from French artistique, an adjective built on artiste; both words go back to Latin ars, whose genitive artis supplies the stem art-. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: artistic 于 18 世纪由法语 artistique 进入英语，该形容词由 artiste 构成；两词都可追溯到拉丁 ars，其属格 artis 提供词干 art-。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ars (genitive artis) meant practical skill, a craft, or a body of rules; a work of beauty was only one of its later applications.
items.cn: ars（属格 artis）意为实用技艺、手艺或一套规则；「美的作品」只是它后来的一项用法。

items.en: Old French artiste of the fourteenth century named a person skilled in an art; the ending -iste marks the agent. It came through Italian artista from Medieval Latin artista.
items.cn: 14 世纪古法语 artiste 指精通某门技艺的人；词尾 -iste 标记施事者。它经意大利语 artista 上溯中世纪拉丁 artista。

items.en: French artistique was formed on artiste as a relational adjective meaning 'belonging to an artist or to art'.
items.cn: 法语 artistique 由 artiste 构成，作关系形容词，意为「属于艺术家或艺术的」。

items.en: English artistic is recorded from 1753, first in the neutral sense 'pertaining to art or artists'.
items.cn: 英语 artistic 自 1753 年有记录，最初是中性的「与艺术或艺术家有关的」。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the word took on the evaluative sense 'showing fine design and execution', and that sense now dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，这个词获得了「设计精良、完成度高」的评价性含义，这一含义如今在日常使用中占主导。

items.en: Reconstructed form: the connection of ars to PIE *ar- 'to fit together' is a reconstruction accepted in standard dictionaries, and no earlier written form survives, so its first spoken date cannot be fixed.
items.cn: 重构形式：ars 与印欧语 *ar-「拼合」的联系是标准辞书接受的重构，更早的书面形式没有留存，因此其最初的口语年代无法确定。

note.en: Group one gathers words built on the same art- stem that are easily swapped in writing; group two gathers adjectives that also praise a result, but from a different angle.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 art- 词干、写作时极易互换的词；第二组是同样在称赞成品、但切入角度不同的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the maker; artistic is the adjective that describes the maker or the work.
entries.definitionCN: 指创作者的名词；artistic 则是描述创作者或作品的形容词。

entries.definition: Built on art in its old sense of skill, but it usually implies cleverness used to deceive, not beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 由 art 的旧义「技艺」构成，但通常暗示用于欺瞒的机巧，而非美。

entries.definition: The negative of artful: natural, sincere, and sometimes clumsy; it does not mean 'without art' in the modern sense.
entries.definitionCN: artful 的反面：自然、真诚，有时显得笨拙；并不表示现代意义上的「没有艺术」。

entries.definition: A colloquial adjective for someone who displays artistic taste conspicuously; the tone is usually mocking.
entries.definitionCN: 口语形容词，指刻意展示艺术品味的人，语气通常带讥讽。

entries.definition: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty; artistic is broader and can also mean 'belonging to the art world'.
entries.definitionCN: 关注美或对美的欣赏；artistic 范围更广，也可指「属于艺术界」。

entries.definition: Stresses producing something new, in or outside art; artistic stresses the trained eye and the field.
entries.definitionCN: 强调产出新东西，可在艺术内外；artistic 强调训练有素的眼光与领域归属。

entries.definition: Says that a choice shows good taste; it makes no claim about skill in making art.
entries.definitionCN: 指某项选择显出好品味；并不声称具备艺术创作技能。

entries.definition: Polished and sensitive, often through upbringing; artistic points to art as the source of that polish.
entries.definitionCN: 文雅而敏感，常来自教养；artistic 则把这种文雅的来源指向艺术。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: artist + -ic: the adjective of relation, so artistic first means 'of artists'.
normal.cn: artist + -ic：关系形容词，因此 artistic 首先是「艺术家的／艺术的」。

normal.en: French artistique (eighteenth century) is the direct model of the English word.
normal.cn: 18 世纪法语 artistique 是英语这个词的直接模板。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the evaluative senses: artistic merit, artistic freedom, artistic licence.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出评价性义项：艺术价值、艺术自由、艺术处理上的自由。

normal.en: The family runs art, artist, artistry, artistic, artistically and arty.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 art、artist、artistry、artistic、artistically 与 arty。

normal.en: A gallery's 'artistic director' is the person who shapes the programme, not the person who paints.
normal.cn: 美术馆的「艺术总监」是决定项目方向的人，不是执笔作画的人。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that stops before adding one more colour, because the empty space already works.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在再加一笔颜色前停住，因为那片留白已经成立。

abstract.en: Picture a fingerprint left on a canvas in strokes rather than lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚留在画布上的指纹，用笔触而不是线条构成。

abstract.en: Picture a person who cannot walk past a badly placed chair without moving it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人路过摆歪的椅子时，总要把它挪正才安心。

examples.en: The city's artistic life depends on small studios as much as on grand museums.
examples.cn: 这座城市的艺术生活既依赖大博物馆，也依赖小工作室。

examples.en: Her artistic judgement was trusted before she had sold a single painting.
examples.cn: 她一幅画都没卖出时，艺术判断力就已得到信任。

examples.en: The director used artistic licence to compress ten years into one evening.
examples.cn: 导演运用艺术上的自由，把十年压缩进一个夜晚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「artist（艺术家）+ -ic」——像艺术家那样讲究 → 有艺术性的

root: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺、手艺、规则体系」；更早词根一般认为是印欧 *ar-「拼合」，属重构形式。英语经古法语 art 与 artiste，1753 年出现 artistic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a neutral label for the field to the qualities of a maker, then to the qualities of a made thing, and finally to the freedom and the temperament popularly assigned to artists.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从对领域的中性标记出发，转到创作者的能力，再转到成品的品质，最后落到人们赋予艺术家的自由与性情。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand arranges pigment, line and empty space into an order that makes people look twice.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把颜料、线条与留白安排成让人愿意多看一会儿的秩序。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the adjective simply points at art as a domain, without praise.
branches.cn: 领域：形容词只指向艺术这一范围，不含褒贬。

branches.en: SKILL AND EYE: one is the power to make, the other the power to notice.
branches.cn: 手艺与眼光：一个是做出来的能力，一个是看出来的能力。

branches.en: QUALITY AND HAND: a good arrangement, then a recognisable personal touch.
branches.cn: 品质与手迹：先有好的安排，再有可辨认的个人手法。

branches.en: FREEDOM: invention first, then the licence to depart from fact.
branches.cn: 自由：先是创造，再是为效果而偏离事实的许可。

branches.en: TEMPERAMENT: the person is read through the mood attributed to the trade.
branches.cn: 性情：人们借助赋予这门手艺的情绪来读这个人。

intro.en: Artistic is a Latin noun plus a Latin-derived adjective suffix, and the same stem builds a large English family of craftsmen, cunning and made things.
intro.cn: artistic 是拉丁名词加拉丁来源的形容词后缀，同一词干还构成一大群表示工匠、机巧与制成品的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars and its stem art- build artifice, artificial, artisan and inert; the last one is the surprise member, since iners literally means 'without skill'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ars 及其词干 art- 构成 artifice、artificial、artisan 与 inert；最后一个是出人意料的成员，因为 iners 字面就是「没有技艺」。

items.meaning: skill; craft; a body of rules
items.example: Art here names the trained ability, not only the finished product.
items.exampleCN: 这里的 art 指训练有素的能力，而不只是成品。

items.example: The suffix turns art into the name of a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 art 变成一个人的名称。

items.example: The artist mixed her own pigments.
items.exampleCN: 这位艺术家自己调配颜料。

items.meaning: belonging to; of the nature of
items.example: The suffix makes a relational adjective from a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由名词构成关系形容词。

items.meaning: of art or artists; showing taste
items.example: The poster shows an artistic hand.
items.exampleCN: 这张海报显出艺术化的手法。

items.example: The room was artistically lit.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间的灯光布置得很有艺术感。

items.example: The restoration shows great artistry.
items.exampleCN: 这次修复展现出高超的技艺。

items.meaning: skilful, often in a cunning way
items.example: An artful answer avoided the question.
items.exampleCN: 一个狡黠的回答绕开了问题。

items.example: Her artless reply was more convincing than a speech.
items.exampleCN: 她那句质朴的回答比一篇演说更有说服力。

items.example: The artisan shaped the bowl by hand.
items.exampleCN: 工匠用手塑出这只碗。

items.example: The plot turns on a harmless artifice.
items.exampleCN: 情节靠一个无伤大雅的巧计推进。

items.meaning: made by art rather than nature
items.example: The lake is artificial but the reeds are real.
items.exampleCN: 这片湖是人工的，芦苇却是真的。

latinEntries.meaning: something made by skill; a cunning device
produced by art, not by nature
latinEntries.meaningCN: 由人工而非自然产生的

latinEntries.meaning: a worker skilled in a craft
latinEntries.meaningCN: 精通某门手艺的劳动者
无技艺的；引申为无生气的、惰性的

definition_zh: 艺术家；（尤指）画家；表演艺术家；能手
definition_en: a person who creates art, especially painting or sculpture, or who performs an art with skill
core_image: 一个人长期把手、眼与材料磨合，最后让材料呈现出只有他能做出的样子
scene: 画室里，学生围住一位正在调色的访客，问她从艺多少年。The students crowded around the visiting artist as she mixed another layer of glaze.
sceneCN: 这里 artist 指「以绘画等造型艺术为业的艺术家」（第 1 个义项：创作绘画或雕塑的人）；句意为学生围住这位来访的艺术家，看她又调上一层釉色。

pos.zh: 艺术家；（尤指）画家、雕塑家；表演艺术家；能手

collocations.zh: 尚未成名的清贫艺术家

forms.label: 借入变体（表演者，常带风格色彩）

derivatives.zh: artist + -ic（关系形容词）→ 艺术的；语义从「人」转到「性质」
artist + -ry（技艺、实践）→ 艺术技巧；从「从业者」转到「手上的功夫」
artist + -e（法语借形）→ 职业表演者；语义偏移为带风格色彩或略带调侃的「艺人」
artist + -hood（身份后缀）→ 艺术家身份；从「人」转到「身份」
art + -less（无）→ 不带机巧的；语义从「技艺」转到「不装腔作势」

senses.title: A maker of paintings or sculpture
senses.definition: a person who makes art, especially by painting or sculpture
senses.definitionCN: 创作艺术的人，尤指通过绘画或雕塑创作的人
senses.example: The gallery represents twelve living artists.
senses.exampleCN: 这家画廊代理十二位在世的艺术家。
senses.why: This is the narrowest and oldest modern sense: the word names the person whose trained hand produces a physical work.
senses.whyCN: 这是最窄也最古老的现代义项：词指的是那个用训练有素的手产出实体作品的人。

senses.title: A performer on stage
senses.definition: a performer in music, dance or theatre
senses.definitionCN: 在音乐、舞蹈或戏剧中表演的人
senses.example: The festival billed her as a sound artist rather than a singer.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐节把她宣传为声音艺术家，而不是歌手。
senses.why: The word widened from makers of objects to makers of performed experience, because both shape an effect for an audience.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从实体作品的制作者扩大到表演体验的创造者，因为两者都在为观众塑造一种效果。

senses.title: A creative maker in any field
senses.definition: a person who creates something with imagination and skill
senses.definitionCN: 以想象力和技艺创造出某物的人
senses.example: She is an artist of the possible, turning limits into designs.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位把限制变成设计的创造者。
senses.why: Once the core is 'skilled making', the object need not be a painting: the word can praise any imaginative construction.
senses.whyCN: 一旦核心是「有技艺的创造」，对象就不必是绘画：这个词可以称赞任何富于想象的构建。

senses.title: An exceptionally skilled practitioner
senses.titleCN: 技艺格外高超的实践者
senses.definition: someone exceptionally skilled at a craft or activity
senses.definitionCN: 在某门手艺或活动中技艺格外高超的人
senses.example: He is an artist with a blade and can fillet a fish in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 他用刀是个高手，几秒钟就能片好一条鱼。
senses.why: The word shifts from art to skill: mastery in any manual practice can be called artistry, so the person becomes an artist of that practice.
senses.whyCN: 词义从「艺术」转到「技艺」：任何手上功夫的精通都可称为 artistry，于是此人就成了那门行当的 artist。

senses.title: A professional in the entertainment industry
senses.titleCN: 娱乐产业中的职业艺人
senses.definition: a performer or recording musician, in industry usage
senses.definitionCN: 行业用语中的表演者或签约音乐人
senses.example: The label signed three new artists last month.
senses.exampleCN: 这家唱片公司上个月签下三位新艺人。
senses.why: Industry language narrows the performer sense to a contractual role: an artist is a person whose performance the company sells.
senses.whyCN: 行业语言把表演者义收窄为一种合约角色：artist 就是公司销售其表演的人。

senses.title: A person who lives by aesthetic values
senses.titleCN: 以审美价值为生活准则的人
senses.definition: someone who orders life around beauty and artistic experience
senses.definitionCN: 以美与艺术体验来安排生活的人
senses.example: He is an artist, not a businessman, and the shop shows it.
senses.exampleCN: 他是艺术家，不是商人，这家店就说明了这一点。
senses.why: From the profession the word borrows a set of values, so a person can be an artist by temperament even without selling work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从职业借来一整套价值观，因此一个人即使不卖作品，也可以凭性情被称作艺术家。

senses.title: The skilled role in a compound
senses.titleCN: 复合词中表示专业角色
senses.definition: the skilled worker in a named activity, as in make-up artist or escape artist
senses.definitionCN: 在化妆师、逃脱术表演者等复合词中，指该活动中技艺娴熟的角色
senses.example: The make-up artist rebuilt the actor's face for the final scene.
senses.exampleCN: 化妆师为最后一场戏重塑了演员的脸。
senses.why: Compounds keep the old sense of 'one skilled in a craft' and attach it to a specific trade, so the artist is the expert in that named task.
senses.whyCN: 复合词保留「精通某门手艺的人」这一旧义，并把它附着到具体行当，因此 artist 就是该任务中的专家。

senses.title: The trickster in 'con artist'
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase con artist, a person who tricks others out of money
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法 con artist 中，指以欺骗骗取钱财的人
senses.example: The con artist sold shares in a mine that did not exist.
senses.exampleCN: 这个骗子出售一座并不存在的矿的股份。
senses.why: The phrase uses artist ironically for 'skilled practitioner': the confidence trick is treated as a craft, so its expert earns the title.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法反讽地把 artist 用作「技艺高超者」：骗局被当成一门手艺，于是其中的高手也获得了这个称号。

intro.en: Artist reached English in the 1580s through French artiste from Italian artista, all built on Latin ars; the older Latin adjective artista meant a craftsman rather than a modern genius. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: artist 于 16 世纪 80 年代经法语 artiste、意大利语 artista 进入英语，根源都是拉丁 ars；更早的拉丁形容词 artista 指工匠，而非现代意义上的天才。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ars (genitive artis) covered practical skill, a craft and a system of rules; beauty was not required by the word itself.
items.cn: ars（属格 artis）涵盖实用技艺、手艺与规则体系；这个词本身并不要求「美」。

items.en: Medieval Latin artista named a person skilled in an art; in classical Latin the same word was closer to 'craftsman, artisan'.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 artista 指精通某门技艺的人；在古典拉丁中，这个词更接近「工匠、手艺人」。

items.en: Italian artista carried the word into the vernacular of the Renaissance workshop, where the painter's skill was being raised above mere craft.
items.cn: 意大利语 artista 把这个词带入文艺复兴工坊的俗语，当时画家的技艺正被提升到单纯手艺之上。

items.en: French artiste of the fourteenth century passed the word to English.
items.cn: 14 世纪的法语 artiste 把这个词传给了英语。

items.en: English artist is recorded in the 1580s meaning 'one who cultivates a fine art'; the modern professional sense settled in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 英语 artist 于 16 世纪 80 年代有记录，意为「研习美术的人」；现代的职业义到 18 世纪才稳定下来。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the word extended to performers, and in the twentieth to recording musicians and other contracted entertainers.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，这个词扩展到表演者；到 20 世纪又扩展到签约音乐人及其他合约艺人。

note.en: Group one holds near neighbours built on the same art- stock that are often confused with artist; group two holds words for people who make or perform, each with a different centre of gravity.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 art- 词干、常与 artist 混淆的近邻；第二组是表示创作者或表演者的词，各自的语义重心不同。

entries.definition: A skilled manual worker, especially in a traditional craft; the word stresses technique and usefulness rather than aesthetic invention.
entries.definitionCN: 熟练的手工劳动者，尤指传统手工艺者；强调技术与实用，而非审美创造。

entries.definition: A French borrowing for a professional performer; in English it often carries a theatrical or slightly mocking tone.
entries.definitionCN: 借自法语的职业表演者称谓；在英语中常带戏剧化或轻微调侃的语气。

entries.definition: The adjective of relation; it describes the person or the work, never the person as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 关系形容词；描述人或作品，但不能作名词指人。

entries.definition: The quality of skilled making; it names what an artist has, not who the artist is.
entries.definitionCN: 指娴熟的创作能力；命名艺术家所具备的东西，而不是艺术家本人。

entries.definition: An artist who works in paint; artist is the wider category that also covers sculptors, printmakers and performers.
entries.definitionCN: 以颜料作画的艺术家；artist 是更广的类别，也涵盖雕塑家、版画家与表演者。

entries.definition: A general word for anyone who brings something into being, including writers and inventors; it lacks the art-world frame.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指使某物产生的人，包括作家与发明者；不带艺术界的框架。

entries.definition: A person who presents an art before an audience; the word stresses the event rather than the making of an object.
entries.definitionCN: 在观众面前呈现艺术的人；强调事件而非物件的制作。

entries.definition: An Italian borrowing for a master of an art, especially music; it is a title of respect, not a job description.
entries.definitionCN: 借自意大利语，指某门艺术的大师，尤指音乐；是尊称，不是职业描述。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: art + -ist 'one who': the person who works in art.
normal.cn: art + -ist「从事者」：在艺术中工作的人。

normal.en: The same -ist builds pianist, novelist and scientist, all names of practitioners.
normal.cn: 同一个 -ist 还构成 pianist、novelist 与 scientist，都是从业者的名称。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: recording artist, make-up artist, con artist.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出词义范围：签约歌手、化妆师、骗子。

normal.en: The family runs art, artistic, artistry, artiste and artless.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 art、artistic、artistry、artiste 与 artless。

normal.en: A studio's 'artist in residence' is a guest who works there for a fixed period.
normal.cn: 工作室的「驻场艺术家」是在那里工作一段固定时间的客人。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that knows the material so well that the material seems to agree with it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手熟悉材料到仿佛材料会顺着它的意思走。

abstract.en: Picture a signature written in a medium that cannot be erased.
abstract.cn: 想象一个用无法擦除的媒材写下的签名。

abstract.en: Picture a person who sees a blank wall as an unfinished sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把一面白墙看成一句没写完的话。

examples.en: The artist spent the morning grinding pigment rather than painting.
examples.cn: 这位艺术家整个上午都在磨颜料，而不是作画。

examples.en: A recording artist may sell millions yet never paint anything.
examples.cn: 一位签约歌手可能卖出数百万张唱片，却从不画画。

examples.en: The con artist relied on charm, not on any actual mine.
examples.cn: 这个骗子靠的是魅力，而不是任何真实存在的矿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「art（艺术）+ -ist（人）」——搞艺术的人 → 艺术家

root: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺、手艺」经中世纪拉丁 artista、意大利语 artista、法语 artiste；artista 在古典拉丁中近于「工匠」，现代「艺术家」义到 18 世纪才稳定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from the person who makes a physical work to the performer, the skilled practitioner, the industry role, the aesthetic temperament, the named specialist and finally the ironic trickster.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从制作实体作品的人出发，依次扩展到表演者、技艺高手、产业角色、审美性情、复合词中的专业角色，最后落到反讽的骗子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person's hand and eye are trained on a material until the material shows what only that person would make.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人的手与眼长期磨合一种材料，直到材料呈现出只有他会做出的样子。

branches.en: MAKING A WORK: the object-maker and the imaginative maker share the core act of shaping something new.
branches.cn: 造物：实体作品的制作者与富于想象的创造者共享「塑形出新物」这一核心动作。

branches.en: STAGE AND INDUSTRY: performance before an audience, then the contractual version of that role.
branches.cn: 舞台与产业：先是面向观众的表演，再是这一角色的合约化版本。

branches.en: SKILL AND SPECIALISM: mastery in a craft, then the named expert inside a compound.
branches.cn: 技艺与专精：先是某门手艺的精通，再是复合词中被点名的专家。

branches.en: TEMPERAMENT: values borrowed from the profession and lived outside it.
branches.cn: 性情：从职业借来的价值观，在职业之外被实践。

branches.en: TRICKSTER: the ironic expert, whose craft is confidence rather than art.
branches.cn: 骗子：反讽意义上的高手，他的手艺是取信而非艺术。

intro.en: Artist is a Latin-derived stem plus the agent suffix -ist, and the same stem supplies a family of nouns, adjectives and verbs about skill and making.
intro.cn: artist 是拉丁来源的词干加施事后缀 -ist，同一词干还提供了一族关于技艺与制作的名词、形容词和动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars, artis is the source; its relatives include artifice, artificial, artisan and inert, while the Greek agent suffix -istēs, latinized as -ista, supplies the ending.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是拉丁 ars、artis；其同族包括 artifice、artificial、artisan 与 inert，而希腊施事后缀 -istēs（拉丁化为 -ista）提供词尾。

items.example: The word began as a name for skill, not for beauty.
items.exampleCN: 这个词最初命名的是技艺，而不是美。

items.example: Pianist and novelist use the same ending.
items.exampleCN: pianist 与 novelist 用的是同一个词尾。

items.example: The word first named a cultivator of a fine art.
items.exampleCN: 这个词最初指研习美术的人。

items.example: The adjective appeared in the eighteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词出现于 18 世纪。

items.example: The carving shows real artistry.
items.exampleCN: 这件雕刻显出真正的技艺。

items.example: The programme lists every artiste in the troupe.
items.exampleCN: 节目单列出了剧团里的每一位艺人。

items.example: An artful pause gave him time to think.
items.exampleCN: 一个巧妙的停顿给了他思考的时间。

items.example: Her artless question exposed the whole plan.
items.exampleCN: 她天真的提问揭穿了整个计划。

items.example: The artisan works in clay and wood.
items.exampleCN: 这位工匠用黏土和木头创作。

items.example: The artificial light flattened the colours.
items.exampleCN: 人造光让色彩显得平淡。

latinEntries.meaning: a made device; a cunning trick
made by art rather than nature
latinEntries.meaningCN: 由人工而非自然造成的
无技艺的；无生气的、惰性的

definition_zh: 艺术作品；（书刊、广告中的）插图与图稿；美术品
definition_en: a work of art, especially a painting, drawing or sculpture, or the illustrations and graphic material prepared for publication
core_image: 一块被反复修改的表面，最后以固定的形状离开工作室，进入别人的眼睛
scene: 印刷厂里，编辑把封面图的文件放大，逐条检查线条。The editor enlarged the artwork to check every line before the press run.
sceneCN: 这里 artwork 指「交给印刷厂的成稿图稿」（第 4 个义项：可供制版复制的图形材料）；句意为编辑把封面图稿放大，在开印前逐条检查线条。

pos.zh: 艺术作品（可数）；插图、图稿（不可数或可数）；美术品

collocations.zh: 封面图稿；封面艺术设计

derivatives.zh: artwork + -ed（分词形容词）→ 经过图稿加工的；从「成品」转到「加工状态」
artwork + -er（人）→ 图稿制作员；从「成品」转到「制作成品的人」
artwork + -ing（动作）→ 图稿制作；从「物件」转到「工序」

senses.title: A single work of art
senses.definition: a painting, drawing, sculpture or similar piece made as art
senses.definitionCN: 作为艺术品创作的绘画、素描、雕塑或类似作品
senses.example: The museum bought the artwork at auction.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆在拍卖会上买下了这件艺术作品。
senses.why: Artwork is simply art plus work, so the compound names a made thing belonging to the category of art: one countable object.
senses.whyCN: artwork 就是 art 加 work，复合词命名一件属于艺术类别的制成品：一个可数的物件。

senses.title: An artist's output as a whole
senses.titleCN: 某位艺术家的全部作品
senses.definition: the collected pieces made by one artist, treated as a body of work
senses.definitionCN: 某位艺术家创作的全部作品，作为一个整体来看
senses.example: The retrospective gathered artwork from forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这场回顾展汇集了四十年的作品。
senses.why: The uncountable use drops the count and keeps the material: the same word now names the whole body rather than one piece.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法取消了计数，只保留「作品实体」：同一个词现在指整个作品群，而不是单件。

senses.title: Illustrations in a publication
senses.definition: the pictures and drawings prepared to accompany printed text
senses.definitionCN: 为配合印刷文字而准备的图画与插图
senses.example: The novel's artwork was drawn by a single illustrator.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的插图全部由一位插画师绘制。
senses.why: Publishing borrowed the word because illustrations are art made to work inside a page: the aesthetic object becomes part of a printed job.
senses.whyCN: 出版业借用这个词，因为插图是「在页面里工作的艺术」：审美对象成了印刷品的一部分。

senses.title: Print-ready graphic material
senses.definition: the finished graphic material supplied to a printer for reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 交给印刷厂用于复制的完成图形材料
senses.example: The editor enlarged the artwork to check every line before the press run.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把封面图稿放大，在开印前逐条检查线条。
senses.why: In the print trade the word narrows to what the press needs: not the idea but the camera-ready surface from which copies are made.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷业中，这个词收窄为印刷机所需之物：不是构思，而是用来复制的那块可制版表面。

senses.title: A digital image or file
senses.definition: an image or layered file made and stored on a computer
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机上制作并保存的图像或分层文件
senses.example: Keep the layered artwork so the type can be changed later.
senses.exampleCN: 保留分层图稿，以便日后修改文字。
senses.why: When production moved to screens, artwork named the editable file rather than the physical surface; the material changed, the function did not.
senses.whyCN: 当制作转移到屏幕上，artwork 指的可编辑文件而非实体表面；材料变了，功能没变。

senses.title: Decoration on a product or package
senses.titleCN: 产品与包装上的装饰图案
senses.definition: the designed pictures or patterns printed on an object or its packaging
senses.definitionCN: 印在物件或其包装上的设计图案
senses.example: The biscuit tin's artwork copies a Victorian print.
senses.exampleCN: 饼干盒上的图案模仿了一幅维多利亚时期的版画。
senses.why: Commercial design applies the print sense to packaging: the image still exists to be reproduced, but now it sells the object beneath it.
senses.whyCN: 商业设计把印刷义用到包装上：图像仍为复制而存在，只是现在用来推销它下面的商品。

senses.title: Visual design for a screen work
senses.titleCN: 影视、游戏等作品的视觉设计
senses.definition: the visual design of a film, game or performance, including concept pieces
senses.definitionCN: 电影、游戏或演出中的视觉设计，包括概念图
senses.example: The game's artwork borrows from woodblock prints.
senses.exampleCN: 这款游戏的视觉设计借鉴了木版画。
senses.why: The word follows images into new media: concept drawings and textures are artworks made to serve a larger screened work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词跟着图像进入新媒介：概念图与贴图都是为更大的屏幕作品服务的图稿。

senses.title: The original object, not a copy
senses.definition: the physical piece made by the artist, as opposed to a reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家亲手制作的实体作品，区别于复制品
senses.example: Collectors pay for the artwork itself, not the poster.
senses.exampleCN: 收藏者付钱买的是原作本身，而不是海报。
senses.why: Because artwork names the made object, museums and dealers use it to insist on the original surface rather than its image.
senses.whyCN: 因为 artwork 命名的是被制作出来的物件，博物馆与画商便用它强调原初表面，而非其图像复制。

intro.en: Artwork is an English compound of art and work, recorded from 1847 and possibly modelled on German Kunstwerk; both parts are old, but the compound is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: artwork 是 art 与 work 的英语复合词，1847 年有记录，可能以德语 Kunstwerk 为模板；两部分都很古老，复合词却是现代产物。年代均为约数。

items.en: Art goes back through Old French to Latin ars, artis 'skill, craft', whose deeper root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: art 经古法语上溯拉丁 ars、artis「技艺、手艺」，其更早词根属重构。

items.en: Work descends from Old English weorc 'deed, something made', from Proto-Germanic *werka- and the root *werg- 'to do'.
items.cn: work 来自古英语 weorc「行为、制成之物」，上溯原始日耳曼语 *werka- 与词根 *werg-「做」。

items.en: German Kunstwerk 'work of art' joins Kunst 'art' and Werk 'work'; the English compound may have followed this model, though the model is not certain.
items.cn: 德语 Kunstwerk「艺术作品」由 Kunst「艺术」与 Werk「作品」合成；英语复合词可能沿此模板，但模板本身并不确定。

items.en: Art-work is recorded in 1847 in the sense 'artistic work; paintings, drawings and similar pieces'.
items.cn: art-work 于 1847 年有记录，意为「艺术性的作品；绘画、素描一类」。

items.en: In twentieth-century printing, artwork narrowed to the finished graphic material from which copies are reproduced.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪的印刷业，artwork 收窄为可供复制成品的图形材料。

items.en: From the late twentieth century the word also names editable image files, extending the old print sense to screens.
items.cn: 从 20 世纪后期起，这个词也指可编辑的图像文件，把旧的印刷义延伸到屏幕。

note.en: Group one separates artwork from art- words that look close but name very different things; group two separates it from words for pictures and designs in other trades.
note.cn: 第一组把 artwork 与看似接近、实则所指完全不同的 art- 词分开；第二组把它与其他行当中表示图画与设计的词分开。

entries.definition: The two-word spelling usually means 'work done in or for art', a task or labour, not a countable piece.
entries.definitionCN: 分写形式通常指「为艺术所做的工作」，是一种劳动或事务，而非可数作品。

entries.definition: An object made by human hands, especially one of archaeological interest; its value lies in evidence, not beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 人手制作的物件，尤指有考古意义的器物；其价值在于证据性，而非美。

entries.definition: A clever made device or a cunning trick; it shares the art- stem but carries deception, not display.
entries.definitionCN: 精巧的装置或狡黠的计谋；同出 art- 词干，却带欺骗而非展示之意。

entries.definition: Skilful in a calculating way; it describes a manner, while artwork names a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 以算计的方式机巧；描述一种方式，而 artwork 命名一个物件。

entries.definition: A picture made to explain or decorate a text; it is a functional category, while artwork can stand alone.
entries.definitionCN: 为解释或装饰文字而作的图画；是功能类别，而 artwork 可以独立存在。

entries.definition: A visual element in design or printing, often commercial; artwork is the broader term that may include fine pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 设计或印刷中的视觉元素，常指商业图形；artwork 更广，可包含纯艺术作品。

entries.definition: A casual word for one work in a gallery or studio; artwork is the explicit term used in catalogues and contracts.
entries.definitionCN: 画廊或工作室中对单件作品的随口说法；artwork 是图录与合同中的明确用语。

entries.definition: The arrangement or plan behind an object; artwork stresses the finished visual surface rather than the planning.
entries.definitionCN: 物件背后的安排或方案；artwork 强调完成的视觉表面，而非计划过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: art + work: a made thing in the category of art.
normal.cn: art + work：艺术类别中的一件制成品。

normal.en: The compound is recorded from 1847 and may follow German Kunstwerk, literally 'art-work'.
normal.cn: 这个复合词 1847 年有记录，可能仿照德语 Kunstwerk，字面就是「艺术-作品」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: original artwork, cover artwork, send artwork to the printer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：原作、封面图稿、把图稿交给印刷厂。

normal.en: The family runs art, work, artwork, artworks and the trade verb artworking.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 art、work、artwork、artworks 以及行业动词 artworking。

normal.en: A printer asks for 'the artwork' when it needs the file, not the framed picture.
normal.cn: 印刷厂要「the artwork」时，要的是文件，不是装框的画。

abstract.en: Picture a surface that keeps the marks of every decision made on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块保留着每一次修改痕迹的表面。

abstract.en: Picture an object that leaves the studio and begins a life in other people's eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一件物品离开工作室，开始在别人的目光里过日子。

abstract.en: Picture a file and a framed canvas answering to the same name.
abstract.cn: 想象一个文件与一幅装框画布回应着同一个名字。

examples.en: The auction catalogue lists every artwork with its provenance.
examples.cn: 拍卖图录列出每件作品及其来源。

examples.en: The magazine's artwork was finished two weeks before the issue closed.
examples.cn: 杂志的图稿在截稿前两周就完成了。

examples.en: She keeps the original artwork in a flat file, away from light.
examples.cn: 她把原作平放在抽屉柜里，避开光线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「art（艺术）+ work（作品）」——艺术做出来的活儿 → 艺术作品

root: art 来自拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺」；work 来自古英语 weorc「所做之事、制成品」，上溯原始日耳曼语 *werka-。二者在 1847 年合为 artwork，可能仿德语 Kunstwerk。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the object from the gallery wall to the printed page, the packaging and the screen, and finally back to the original surface that copies cannot replace.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让这件物品从画廊墙面走到印刷页、包装与屏幕，最后回到复制品无法替代的原作表面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface is revised again and again until it leaves the studio as a fixed shape and enters other people's eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块表面被反复修改，直到以固定形状离开工作室，进入别人的眼睛。

branches.en: THE OBJECT AND THE ORIGINAL: one countable piece, and the insistence that it is not a copy.
branches.cn: 物件与原作：一件可数作品，以及对「它不是复制品」的坚持。

branches.en: THE OEUVRE: the same word without a count gathers a whole life's making.
branches.cn: 作品群：去掉计数后，同一个词收拢一生的创作。

branches.en: THE PRINTED PAGE: illustration first, then the material handed to the press.
branches.cn: 印刷页：先是插图，再是交给印刷机的材料。

branches.en: THE FILE: the editable image inherits the print function on a screen.
branches.cn: 文件：可编辑图像在屏幕上继承了印刷功能。

branches.en: COMMERCIAL SURFACES: packaging and screen works put the image to work.
branches.cn: 商业表面：包装与屏幕作品让图像去干活。

intro.en: Artwork is a transparent English compound, so both halves can be read separately, and each half has its own family.
intro.cn: artwork 是一个透明的英语复合词，两半都能单独读，而且各自都有自己的词族。

latinIntro.en: Only the first half has a Latin ancestor, ars; the second half is native Germanic, and the compound itself is modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前半有拉丁祖先 ars；后半是日耳曼本族词，复合词本身则是现代英语的产物。

items.example: Art supplies the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: art 提供这个复合词的前半。

items.example: Work supplies the second half.
items.exampleCN: work 提供后半。

items.example: The gallery hung the artwork badly.
items.exampleCN: 画廊把这件作品挂得很糟。

items.example: The crate held six artworks.
items.exampleCN: 箱子里装了六件作品。

items.example: The artworker fixed the spacing before printing.
items.exampleCN: 图稿制作员在印刷前调整了字距。

items.example: Artworking took longer than the design.
items.exampleCN: 图稿制作比设计本身更耗时。

items.example: The phrase is older than the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语比复合词更古老。

items.example: The dig catalogued every artefact.
items.exampleCN: 发掘记录了每一件器物。

items.example: The artisan signed the table.
items.exampleCN: 工匠在桌上签了名。

definition_zh: 艺术史；艺术史学科；（某一时期或地区的）艺术发展史
definition_en: the academic study of the history and development of the visual arts, or the history of art in a particular period or place
core_image: 一排按年代挂起的画，被一条关于风格、赞助与观看方式的线索穿起来
scene: 讲堂的屏幕上，两幅相隔百年的画被并排放置，学生被要求找出构图的变化。The lecture used two paintings a century apart to show how art history compares styles.
sceneCN: 这里 art history 指「作为学科的艺术史」（第 1 个义项：系统研究艺术发展及其方法的学问）；句意为这堂课用相隔一个世纪的两幅画，说明艺术史如何比较风格。

pos.zh: 艺术史；艺术史学科（通常不可数，特定叙述时可数）

forms.label: 可数用法（少见，指多种叙述）

derivatives.zh: art history + -an（从业者）→ 艺术史学者；从「学科」转到「研究该学科的人」
art history + -al（关系形容词）→ 艺术史的；从「领域」转到「属性」
history + -ic（关系形容词）→ 有历史意义的；从「记录」转到「值得记录」
historic + -ally（副词后缀）→ 在历史上；从「性质」转到「观察角度」
history + -an（人）→ 历史学家；从「叙述」转到「写叙述的人」

senses.title: The academic discipline
senses.definition: the scholarly study of art and its development, with its own methods and questions
senses.definitionCN: 对艺术及其发展进行学术研究，并形成自身方法与问题的学科
senses.example: She studied art history in Florence.
senses.exampleCN: 她在佛罗伦萨学习艺术史。
senses.why: The compound joins a subject (art) to a method of inquiry (history), so the name denotes the discipline that applies historical questions to works of art.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把对象「艺术」与探究方式「历史」连接起来，因此命名的是把历史问题用于艺术作品的学科。

senses.title: A course or programme
senses.definition: a class or programme in this field
senses.definitionCN: 该领域的一门课程或培养项目
senses.example: Art history is a required course for the major.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术史是这个专业的必修课。
senses.why: A discipline taught becomes a course, so the same name can denote the slot in a timetable rather than the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 被教授的一门学科会成为课程，因此同一个名称也能指课表上的一个位置，而不是整个领域。

senses.title: The actual development of art
senses.definition: the history of art as it happened, independent of how it is studied
senses.definitionCN: 艺术实际发生的历史，不依赖人们如何研究它
senses.example: The art history of the period is one of rapid experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 这一时期的艺术史充满快速实验。
senses.why: History can mean the events themselves, not only the study of them; the compound inherits both readings from its second element.
senses.whyCN: history 既可指事件本身，也可指对事件的研究；复合词从第二个成分继承了这两种读法。

senses.title: A particular written account
senses.titleCN: 关于艺术发展的一种叙述
senses.definition: a book or account that narrates the development of art
senses.definitionCN: 叙述艺术发展的一部书或一种说法
senses.example: His book offers a new art history of the interwar years.
senses.exampleCN: 他的书提供了两次大战之间年代的一种新艺术史叙述。
senses.why: Every history is also a telling, so the compound can name one narrative among rivals rather than the objective sequence.
senses.whyCN: 每一种历史也是一种叙述，因此复合词能指与竞争叙述并列的一种讲法，而不是客观序列。

senses.title: Art history of a place or period
senses.titleCN: 某地或某时期的艺术史
senses.definition: the history of art in a specified region, period or tradition
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区、时期或传统中的艺术史
senses.example: The art history of Venice is inseparable from its trade.
senses.exampleCN: 威尼斯的艺术史与它的贸易密不可分。
senses.why: Restricting the compound with of or a place-name turns the whole discipline into a bounded subject: this art history, here.
senses.whyCN: 用 of 或地名限定这个复合词，就把整门学科变成一个有限对象：此地的这一段艺术史。

senses.title: The scholarly literature
senses.definition: the body of published research on a work, artist or question
senses.definitionCN: 关于某件作品、某位艺术家或某个问题的已发表研究总体
senses.example: The art history on this workshop fills three shelves.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这个工坊的艺术史研究文献装满了三层书架。
senses.why: The discipline is also the sum of what has been written; the uncountable use shifts from activity to accumulated text.
senses.whyCN: 学科也是已写成之物总和；不可数用法从「活动」转到「累积的文本」。

senses.title: A method of visual analysis
senses.definition: a method of analysing works through their forms, materials and visual structure
senses.definitionCN: 通过形式、材料与视觉结构分析作品的方法
senses.example: Formal art history begins with a close reading of the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 形式分析的艺术史从对画面的细读开始。
senses.why: Because the discipline developed distinct techniques, its name can stand for the technique itself, especially when contrasted with theory or criticism.
senses.whyCN: 由于这门学科发展出多种技术，其名称也可指技术本身，尤其在与理论或批评对照时。

senses.title: A department or scholarly community
senses.definition: the institutional unit or community of scholars working in the field
senses.definitionCN: 从事该领域工作的院系单位或学者群体
senses.example: The art history department shares a building with the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术史系与博物馆共用一栋楼。
senses.why: Metonymy turns the subject into the people and rooms that teach it: the department is called by the name of its field.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把学科变成教授它的人与房间：院系用其领域的名称来称呼。

intro.en: Art history joins two old words, Latin ars and Greek historia, into a modern compound; the discipline took shape in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: art history 把两个古老的词——拉丁 ars 与希腊 historia——合成一个现代复合词；这门学科在 19 世纪成形。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ars, artis meant practical skill, a craft, or a system of rules; the modern category of fine art grew out of this word.
items.cn: ars、artis 意为实用技艺、手艺或规则体系；现代「美术」这一类别就是从这个词生长出来的。

items.en: Greek historia meant 'inquiry, learning by investigation, a written account'; it came from histōr 'witness, judge'.
items.cn: 希腊 historia 意为「探究、通过调查获得的知识、书面叙述」，来自 histōr「见证者、评判者」。

items.en: Latin borrowed historia as a narrative of events; Old French histoire and Middle English history carried it into English.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 historia，指对事件的叙述；古法语 histoire 与中古英语 history 把它带入英语。

items.en: Art history is a modern English compound: the object plus the inquiry. Similar compounds such as natural history and church history were already established.
items.cn: art history 是现代英语复合词：对象加探究方式。natural history、church history 等类似复合词此前已经确立。

items.en: Universities, museums and printed catalogues turned the study of art's past into a taught discipline with chairs, journals and methods.
items.cn: 大学、博物馆与印刷图录把对艺术过去的研究变成有教席、期刊与方法的可授学科。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): no single first citation for the compound is agreed, and the boundary between antiquarian description and art history is itself debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个复合词没有公认的最早书证，而且古物描述与艺术史之间的界线本身也有争议。

note.en: Group one holds the academic labels most often swapped with art history; group two holds neighbouring ways of studying art that ask different questions.
note.cn: 第一组是最常与 art history 混用的学科名称；第二组是研究艺术但问题不同的邻近路径。

entries.definition: The scholar who works in the field; art history is the field itself.
entries.definitionCN: 在该领域工作的学者；art history 是领域本身。

entries.definition: The evaluation of works, usually present-tense; art history reconstructs their place in time.
entries.definitionCN: 对作品的评价，通常是当下时态；艺术史则重建作品在时间中的位置。

entries.definition: The conceptual framework for understanding art; it need not follow dates or provenance.
entries.definitionCN: 理解艺术的概念框架；不必按年代或来源展开。

entries.definition: General instruction in how to look at and enjoy art, usually without original research.
entries.definitionCN: 教人如何观看与欣赏艺术的通识课程，通常不含原创研究。

entries.definition: The study of all visual media, including advertising and scientific images; art history keeps the fine-art core.
entries.definitionCN: 研究一切视觉媒介，包括广告与科学图像；艺术史保留美术核心。

entries.definition: The study of museums, collecting and display; it uses art history but focuses on institutions.
entries.definitionCN: 研究博物馆、收藏与展示；会使用艺术史，但焦点在机构。

entries.definition: The expert judgement of authorship, date and quality; a handmaid to art history rather than the whole discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 对作者、年代与品质的专家判断；是艺术史的辅助技艺，而非整门学科。

entries.definition: The history of beliefs and practices, of which art may be one source; art history keeps works at the centre.
entries.definitionCN: 信念与实践的历史，艺术只是其中一种材料；艺术史把作品放在中心。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: art + history: the history of art, then the discipline that writes it.
normal.cn: art + history：艺术的历史，然后是书写这段历史的学科。

normal.en: history goes back to Greek historia 'inquiry'; the discipline is an inquiry, not a list of dates.
normal.cn: history 上溯希腊 historia「探究」；这门学科是探究，不是年表。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: art history department, art history survey, a degree in art history.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：艺术史系、艺术史通史课、艺术史学位。

normal.en: The family runs art, history, historian, art historian and art historical.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 art、history、historian、art historian 与 art historical。

normal.en: A museum label often gives the 'art historical' date, while the wall text gives the criticism.
normal.cn: 博物馆标签常给出「艺术史」年代，墙面说明则给出评论。

abstract.en: Picture paintings hung in a row, each one turning to face the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一排挂起的画，每幅都转过来面对下一幅。

abstract.en: Picture a timeline drawn through a gallery rather than along a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一条时间线穿过画廊，而不是画在纸页上。

abstract.en: Picture a question mark placed over a finished masterpiece.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问号落在一件已完成的杰作上。

examples.en: Art history asks not only what a work looks like but who paid for it.
examples.cn: 艺术史不只问作品长什么样，还问是谁出钱做的。

examples.en: The department teaches art history alongside conservation and museum studies.
examples.cn: 该系把艺术史与修复、博物馆研究放在一起教授。

examples.en: Her art history of the region begins with a single church door.
examples.cn: 她写的该地区艺术史从一扇教堂门开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「art（艺术）+ history（历史）」——给艺术写的历史 → 艺术史

root: art 来自拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺」；history 来自希腊 historia「探究、叙述」，经拉丁 historia 与古法语 histoire。二者合成现代英语复合词 art history，19 世纪成为学科。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses separate the discipline from its course, its actual past, its narratives, its literature, its method and its institutional home.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把学科与课程、实际过去、叙述、文献、方法及机构归属分开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of paintings is threaded by one line about style, patronage and the way viewers looked.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排画被一条关于风格、赞助与观看方式的线索穿起来。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND ITS HOME: the discipline as knowledge, then the department that teaches it.
branches.cn: 学科及其归属：先作为知识的学科，再是教授它的院系。

branches.en: THE COURSE: the discipline cut down to a timetable slot.
branches.cn: 课程：学科被切成课表上的一个位置。

branches.en: WHAT HAPPENED: the events themselves, before any account is written.
branches.cn: 实际发生：在任何叙述写成之前的事件本身。

branches.en: ACCOUNTS, LITERATURE AND METHOD: one telling, the accumulated shelf of tellings, and the trained way of reading form.
branches.cn: 叙述、文献与方法：一种讲法，累积成架的各种讲法，以及阅读形式的训练有素的方法。

branches.en: A BOUNDED SUBJECT: the whole discipline restricted to one place or period.
branches.cn: 有限对象：整门学科被限定到一地或一时。

intro.en: The phrase is a transparent compound of a Latin-derived noun and a Greek-derived noun, so both halves can be read with their own histories.
intro.cn: 这个短语是拉丁来源名词与希腊来源名词的透明复合词，两半都能连同自身历史一起读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies ars for the first half and historia, borrowed from Greek, for the second; historia itself comes from Greek histōr 'witness'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语为前半提供 ars，为后半提供借自希腊语的 historia；historia 本身来自希腊 histōr「见证者」。

items.example: Art names the object studied.
items.exampleCN: art 命名被研究的对象。

items.structure: Greek historia (inquiry, account), through Latin and Old French
items.meaning: an inquiry into the past; a narrative
items.example: History names the method.
items.exampleCN: history 命名方法。

items.example: Art history began to be taught in universities.
items.exampleCN: 艺术史开始在大学里被教授。

items.meaning: a person connected with a field
items.example: Historian uses the same ending.
items.exampleCN: historian 用的是同一个词尾。

items.example: The art historian dated the panel by its frame.
items.exampleCN: 这位艺术史学者通过画框为木板画定年。

items.example: The question is art historical, not chemical.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题属于艺术史，而不是化学。

items.meaning: a writer or researcher of history
items.example: The historian checked the inventory.
items.exampleCN: 历史学家核对了清单。

items.meaningCN: 历史上有重要意义的；有记载的
items.example: The sale was a historic event for the museum.
items.exampleCN: 这次收购对博物馆是历史性事件。

items.meaning: relating to the past as recorded
items.meaningCN: 与有记载的过去有关的
items.example: The building has historical value.
items.exampleCN: 这座建筑有历史价值。

latinEntries.meaning: inquiry; a written account of events
latinEntries.meaningCN: 探究；对事件的书面叙述

latinEntries.meaning: a craftsman; a maker by skill

definition_zh: 美学；审美观；（事物给人的）美感、外观设计
definition_en: the branch of philosophy concerned with beauty and art, or the visual qualities and style of something
core_image: 一个人在看一件东西时先被它的样子打动，再追问自己为什么被打动
scene: 展厅里，观众先注意到墙面颜色与灯光，然后才读作品说明。The new gallery's aesthetics put the visitor's eye before the label.
sceneCN: 这里 aesthetics 指「空间给人的整体视觉风格与美感」（第 3 个义项：某物的外观与视觉品质）；句意为这座新画廊的视觉设计让观众先看，再读标签。

pos.zh: 美学（学科，作单数）；审美观（可作复数意义）；外观美感

derivatives.zh: aesthetics 去掉 -s → 审美的；从「学科」回到「性质」
aesthetic + -ally（副词）→ 在审美上；从「性质」转到「评价方式」
aesthetic + -e（人）→ 审美者；从「感知」转到「以美为价值的人」
aesthetic + -ism（主义）→ 唯美主义；从「审美」转到「把美当作最高价值的主张」
an-（无）+ aisthēsis（感知）→ 麻醉；同根但语义相反：从「感知」转到「失去感知」

senses.title: The philosophy of beauty and art
senses.titleCN: 研究美与艺术的哲学分支
senses.definition: the branch of philosophy that studies beauty, art and taste
senses.definitionCN: 研究美、艺术与趣味的哲学分支
senses.example: Aesthetics asks what makes an object beautiful.
senses.exampleCN: 美学追问是什么让一件物品成为美的。
senses.why: The name was coined for a science of sensory knowledge; as philosophy took it up, the field narrowed to beauty, art and the judgement of taste.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称最初指关于感官知识的科学；哲学接管后，领域收窄到美、艺术与趣味判断。

senses.title: The study of sensory perception
senses.titleCN: 对感官感知的研究（原义）
senses.definition: the original sense: the study of perception through the senses
senses.definitionCN: 原初义：研究通过感官获得的感知
senses.example: Baumgarten founded aesthetics as the science of sensory perception.
senses.exampleCN: 鲍姆加登把美学建立为研究感官感知的科学。
senses.why: Greek aisthēsis is 'perception', so the first coinage named a theory of sensory experience before it named a theory of beauty.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 aisthēsis 是「感知」，因此最初的造词命名的是感官经验理论，而不是美的理论。

senses.title: The visual character of an object
senses.titleCN: 某物的外观与视觉品质
senses.definition: the visual qualities and overall look of a building, object or space
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、物件或空间的视觉品质与整体观感
senses.example: The new gallery's aesthetics put the visitor's eye before the label.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新画廊的视觉设计让观众先看，再读标签。
senses.why: From the study of perception the word slid to the perceived quality itself: what the eye meets can be called its aesthetics.
senses.whyCN: 从对感知的研究，词义滑向被感知的品质本身：眼睛所遇之物就可以被称为它的 aesthetics。

senses.title: The design principles of a movement
senses.titleCN: 某个流派或时代的设计原则
senses.definition: the set of visual principles associated with a movement or period
senses.definitionCN: 与某个流派或时期相关的一套视觉原则
senses.example: Modernist aesthetics favoured clean lines and exposed structure.
senses.exampleCN: 现代主义美学偏爱干净的线条与外露的结构。
senses.why: A movement is a shared way of seeing, so its principles can be summed up as an aesthetics: a doctrine of what looks right.
senses.whyCN: 流派是一种共享的观看方式，因此其原则可总括为一种 aesthetics：关于什么看起来正确的信条。

senses.title: A personal system of taste
senses.definition: a person's or group's set of preferences about beauty
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体关于美的偏好集合
senses.example: His aesthetics are severe: no ornament, no colour.
senses.exampleCN: 他的审美很严厉：不要装饰，不要色彩。
senses.why: The discipline's name becomes countable in use: each person can hold a small theory of beauty, and that theory is called their aesthetics.
senses.whyCN: 学科名称在使用中变得可数：每个人都能持有一套关于美的小理论，这套理论就叫他的 aesthetics。

senses.title: Beauty as a selling point
senses.definition: the aesthetic appeal of a product, treated as a commercial quality
senses.definitionCN: 产品在审美上的吸引力，被当作商业品质
senses.example: The phone's aesthetics matter as much as its battery.
senses.exampleCN: 这部手机的外观美感与电池同样重要。
senses.why: Industry turned the word into a market attribute: a product is judged by how it looks, and that looks is its aesthetics.
senses.whyCN: 产业把这个词变成市场属性：产品按外观被评判，而外观就是它的 aesthetics。

senses.title: The look of a screen or game
senses.titleCN: 屏幕作品或游戏的视觉风格
senses.definition: the distinctive visual style of a film, game or interface
senses.definitionCN: 电影、游戏或界面的独特视觉风格
senses.example: The game's retro aesthetics borrow from early arcade cabinets.
senses.exampleCN: 这款游戏的复古视觉风格借鉴了早期街机框体。
senses.why: Digital media inherited the commercial sense and narrowed it to style: the whole look, not one beautiful object, is now the aesthetics.
senses.whyCN: 数字媒介继承了商业义并把它收窄为风格：整套外观，而不是单件美物，如今成了 aesthetics。

senses.title: Beauty in nature and environment
senses.definition: the aesthetic qualities of landscapes and environments, as a field of study
senses.definitionCN: 景观与环境的审美品质，作为研究领域
senses.example: Environmental aesthetics studies the beauty of coasts and forests.
senses.exampleCN: 环境美学研究海岸与森林之美。
senses.why: The discipline extended its questions from artworks to the natural world, so landscapes can have an aesthetics of their own.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科把问题从艺术品扩展到自然世界，因此景观也可以有自己的 aesthetics。

intro.en: Aesthetics was coined in modern philosophy from Greek aisthēsis 'perception' and entered English around 1800 through German and French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: aesthetics 由近代哲学用希腊 aisthēsis「感知」造成，约 1800 年经德语与法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aisthēsis meant 'perception by the senses'; the verb aisthanesthai meant 'to perceive, feel'.
items.cn: aisthēsis 意为「通过感官的感知」；动词 aisthanesthai 意为「感知、感受」。

items.en: Aisthētikos meant 'of or for sense perception, perceptible'; it supplied the adjective behind the modern noun.
items.cn: aisthētikos 意为「与感官感知有关的、可感知的」，为现代名词提供了形容词基础。

items.en: Alexander Baumgarten coined Ästhetik in the eighteenth century for the science of sensuous knowledge; Kant used the term for the conditions of perception.
items.cn: 亚历山大·鲍姆加登于 18 世纪造出 Ästhetik，指关于感官知识的科学；康德用这个词指感知的条件。

items.en: English aesthetic is recorded from 1798 and aesthetics from 1803, both from German or French models.
items.cn: 英语 aesthetic 自 1798 年有记录，aesthetics 自 1803 年有记录，均来自德语或法语模板。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the term moved from sensory perception to the criticism of taste, and beauty became its central question.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，这个词从感官感知转到趣味批评，美成为其核心问题。

items.en: Reconstructed form: the deeper root of aisthanesthai is given as PIE *au- 'to perceive', a reconstruction with no surviving written witness.
items.cn: 重构形式：aisthanesthai 的更早词根被拟为印欧 *au-「感知」，这一重构没有留存的书面证据。

note.en: Group one holds the aisth- family, including a medical word that looks like its opposite; group two holds neighbouring ways of talking about beauty and style.
note.cn: 第一组是 aisth- 词族，其中还包括一个看似反义的医学词；第二组是谈论美与风格的邻近说法。

entries.definition: The adjective 'concerning beauty', or a noun for one principle of taste; aesthetics is the field or the overall look.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「关于美的」，或名词指一条审美原则；aesthetics 是学科或整体观感。

entries.definition: A person devoted to beauty and refined taste; the word often suggests cultivated sensibility.
entries.definitionCN: 献身于美与精致品味的人；常暗示有教养的感受力。

entries.definition: The belief that beauty should be valued for itself, especially the art-for-art's-sake movement.
entries.definitionCN: 认为美应因其自身而被珍视的主张，尤指「为艺术而艺术」运动。

entries.definition: Loss of sensation, especially under medical anaesthetic; an- 'without' plus aisthēsis 'perception' makes it the exact negative of the root.
entries.definitionCN: 感觉丧失，尤指麻醉状态；an-「无」加 aisthēsis「感知」，使它正好是这个词根的反义。

entries.definition: The philosophical study of art, including questions of meaning and ontology; aesthetics is its older and often narrower name.
entries.definitionCN: 对艺术的哲学研究，包括意义与存在问题；aesthetics 是更古老、通常也更窄的名称。

entries.definition: The practice of evaluating particular works; it applies aesthetic ideas but is not the theory itself.
entries.definitionCN: 评价具体作品的实践；会应用美学观念，但本身不是理论。

entries.definition: The ability to discern what is good or beautiful; aesthetics studies taste, while taste is the capacity being studied.
entries.definitionCN: 辨别何为好或美的能力；美学研究趣味，而趣味是被研究的能力。

entries.definition: A characteristic way of making or appearing; aesthetics is the broader inquiry into why a style pleases.
entries.definitionCN: 制作或呈现的独特方式；aesthetics 是追问一种风格为何令人愉悦的更广研究。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek aisthēsis 'perception' + -ics 'the study of': the study of what the senses take in.
normal.cn: 希腊 aisthēsis「感知」+ -ics「……学」：研究感官接收到的东西。

normal.en: Baumgarten coined the German term in the eighteenth century for sensory knowledge, not for beauty alone.
normal.cn: 鲍姆加登在 18 世纪造出德语术语，指感官知识，而不只是美。

normal.en: The pair aesthetic and anesthesia share the root: one turns perception on, the other off.
normal.cn: aesthetic 与 anesthesia 共享词根：一个打开感知，一个关闭感知。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the modern uses: visual aesthetics, the aesthetics of a building, environmental aesthetics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出今用：视觉美学、建筑外观、环境美学。

normal.en: The family runs aesthetic, aesthetics, aesthete, aestheticism and aesthetically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 aesthetic、aesthetics、aesthete、aestheticism 与 aesthetically。

abstract.en: Picture an eye that feels first and asks questions afterwards.
abstract.cn: 想象一只先感受、后提问的眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a room whose colours seem to decide how you stand in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，颜色似乎决定了你站立的方式。

abstract.en: Picture a switch that can turn feeling off, which is what anesthesia does.
abstract.cn: 想象一个能把感觉关掉的开关，麻醉做的正是这件事。

examples.en: Aesthetics and ethics are separate questions, though artists often mix them.
examples.cn: 美学与伦理是两个问题，尽管艺术家常把它们混在一起。

examples.en: The car was redesigned for aesthetics rather than for luggage space.
examples.cn: 这款车重新设计是为了外观美感，而不是行李空间。

examples.en: She wrote on the aesthetics of everyday objects rather than on painting.
examples.cn: 她写的是日常物品的审美，而不是绘画。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「aes（近似「爱死」）+ thetics」——爱到极致的感受 → 美学

root: 希腊 aisthēsis「感知」、aisthētikos「可感知的」；鲍姆加登 18 世纪以 Ästhetik 指感官知识之学，英语 aesthetic 1798 年、aesthetics 1803 年。更早词根拟为印欧 *au-「感知」，属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the philosophy of beauty back to its original study of perception, then out to the look of objects, movements, products, screens and landscapes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从美的哲学出发，回到最初的感知研究，再向外扩展到物件、流派、产品、屏幕与景观的外观。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person is first moved by how something looks, then asks why it moved them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人先被某物的样子打动，再追问自己为什么被打动。

branches.en: THE STUDY AND ITS ROOT: beauty as a philosophical question, then perception as the older subject.
branches.cn: 学科及其根：美作为哲学问题，然后是更早的感知主题。

branches.en: WHAT THE EYE MEETS: an object's look, and the look of a whole landscape.
branches.cn: 眼睛所遇：一件物件的外观，以及整片景观的外观。

branches.en: SHARED PRINCIPLES: a movement turns private taste into a doctrine of form.
branches.cn: 共享原则：流派把私人趣味变成关于形式的信条。

branches.en: PRIVATE TASTE: each person carries a small theory of what looks right.
branches.cn: 私人趣味：每个人都带着一套关于「什么看起来对」的小理论。

branches.en: SOLD AND SCREENED: appearance becomes a product feature and then a whole digital style.
branches.cn: 被售卖与被投影：外观先成为产品卖点，再成为整套数字风格。

intro.en: Aesthetics is a Greek root plus a Greek-derived suffix of study; the same root builds the adjective, the person and the medical negative.
intro.cn: aesthetics 是希腊词根加希腊来源的「学问」后缀；同一词根还构成形容词、指人的名词与医学上的反义词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here: the word is Greek aisthēsis plus -ics, and Latin only transmitted Greek philosophy into modern languages.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁祖先：词由希腊 aisthēsis 加 -ics 构成，拉丁语只把希腊哲学传给了现代语言。

items.example: The root concerns feeling, not beauty as such.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根关心的是感受，而不是美本身。

items.meaning: a field of study or practice
items.example: Physics and ethics use the same ending.
items.exampleCN: physics 与 ethics 用的是同一个词尾。

items.example: The noun supplies the stem of the modern term.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供现代术语的词干。

items.meaning: the study of perception, later of beauty
items.example: Aesthetics became a university subject.
items.exampleCN: 美学成为一门大学学科。

items.example: The aesthetic judgement came before the price.
items.exampleCN: 审美判断先于价格出现。

items.example: The bridge is aesthetically successful.
items.exampleCN: 这座桥在审美上是成功的。

items.example: The aesthete refused to own an ugly chair.
items.exampleCN: 这位审美者拒绝拥有一把难看的椅子。

items.meaning: devotion to beauty for its own sake
items.example: Aestheticism shaped the decade's interiors.
items.exampleCN: 唯美主义塑造了那个年代的室内风格。

items.example: The drug produces anesthesia.
items.exampleCN: 这种药使人失去感觉。

definition_zh: 唯美主义；审美崇拜；为艺术而艺术的主张
definition_en: the belief that art should be valued for beauty alone, especially the late nineteenth-century movement of art for art's sake
core_image: 一间把实用物件全部移走、只留下颜色与线条的房间
scene: 展厅里，导览说这批画家拒绝让画承担道德说教，只谈颜色与形状。The guide explained that aestheticism rejected any moral duty for painting.
sceneCN: 这里 aestheticism 指「主张艺术只应追求美、不承担道德或实用任务的理论」（第 2 个义项：为艺术而艺术的信条）；句意为导览说明唯美主义拒绝让绘画承担道德义务。

pos.zh: 唯美主义；审美崇拜（通常不可数）

collocations.zh: 维多利亚时期的唯美主义
19 世纪 90 年代的唯美主义
为艺术而艺术的唯美主义

forms.label: 可数用法（少见，指多种形态）

derivatives.zh: 希腊 aisthētikos「可感知的」→ 审美的；从「感知」转到「美」
aesthetic + -ics（学问）→ 美学；从「性质」转到「学科」
aesthetic + -e（人）→ 审美者；从「性质」转到「以美为价值的人」
aestheticism + -ist（信奉者）→ 唯美主义者；从「主义」转到「持此主张的人」
aesthetic + -ize（使……化）→ 使带上审美色彩；从「性质」转到「施加动作」

senses.title: The late nineteenth-century movement
senses.titleCN: 19 世纪后期的唯美主义运动
senses.definition: the late Victorian movement that made beauty the chief aim of art and life
senses.definitionCN: 维多利亚后期把美作为艺术与生活首要目标的运动
senses.example: The novel is usually read as a document of aestheticism.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说通常被读作唯美主义的一份文献。
senses.why: The suffix -ism names a movement as well as a doctrine, so aestheticism can denote the historical circle around Pater and Wilde.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ism 既可命名主张，也可命名运动，因此 aestheticism 能指佩特与王尔德周围的那个历史圈子。

senses.title: Art for art's sake
senses.definition: the principle that art owes nothing to morality, utility or social purpose
senses.definitionCN: 艺术不对道德、实用或社会目的负有任何义务的原则
senses.example: Aestheticism holds that art owes no moral lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 唯美主义认为艺术不欠任何道德教训。
senses.why: The movement's core claim is that beauty is the only end of art; the name of the movement became the name of that claim.
senses.whyCN: 这场运动的核心主张是美是艺术的唯一目的；运动的名称于是成了这条主张的名称。

senses.title: Devotion to beauty as a value
senses.definition: a personal commitment to beauty as the highest good
senses.definitionCN: 把美视为最高善的个人承诺
senses.example: Her aestheticism extended to the arrangement of a dinner table.
senses.exampleCN: 她的唯美追求连餐桌的摆法都不放过。
senses.why: A doctrine can become a temperament: when someone lives by the primacy of beauty, the word describes the commitment rather than a movement.
senses.whyCN: 主张可以变成性情：当一个人按美的优先性生活，这个词描述的就是这种承诺，而不是一场运动。

senses.title: Life treated as a work of art
senses.definition: the attitude that experience itself should be shaped aesthetically
senses.definitionCN: 认为经验本身应按审美方式塑造的态度
senses.example: Pater's aestheticism treated life itself as a work of art.
senses.exampleCN: 佩特的唯美主义把生活本身当作艺术品。
senses.why: If art needs no purpose outside beauty, then a life can be composed like an artwork; the doctrine extends from objects to conduct.
senses.whyCN: 如果艺术在美之外无需目的，那么生活也可以像艺术品一样被经营；主张因此从物件扩展到行为。

senses.title: A decorative style
senses.definition: the visual style associated with the aesthetic movement, especially in interiors and dress
senses.definitionCN: 与唯美运动相关的视觉风格，尤见于室内与服饰
senses.example: The house is a monument of eighteen-nineties aestheticism.
senses.exampleCN: 这座房子是 19 世纪 90 年代唯美主义风格的纪念碑。
senses.why: A movement leaves objects behind; its characteristic palette and patterns come to be called by the movement's name.
senses.whyCN: 运动会在物件上留下痕迹；其特有的色彩与纹样便被以运动之名相称。

senses.title: Over-concern with appearance
senses.titleCN: 对外观的过度讲究（贬义）
senses.definition: a pejorative term for excessive attention to surface beauty
senses.definitionCN: 贬义用法，指对表面之美的过度关注
senses.example: Critics attacked the aestheticism of the campaign as mere decoration.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抨击这场宣传活动只是装饰性的唯美做派。
senses.why: Any value can be mocked when it looks like evasion; aestheticism became a label for prettiness that avoids harder questions.
senses.whyCN: 任何价值在被视为逃避时都可能被讥讽；aestheticism 成了「只顾好看、回避难题」的标签。

senses.title: A stance in literary criticism
senses.titleCN: 文学批评中的一种立场
senses.definition: an approach that judges literature by formal beauty rather than moral or social effect
senses.definitionCN: 按形式之美而非道德或社会效果来评判文学的路径
senses.example: His aestheticism shaped a generation of literary criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 他的唯美立场塑造了一代文学批评。
senses.why: Literary criticism borrowed the movement's name for a method: reading for form, texture and pleasure rather than message.
senses.whyCN: 文学批评借用了这场运动的名字来命名一种方法：为形式、质感与愉悦而读，而非为信息而读。

senses.title: Beauty as the chief criterion in a field
senses.titleCN: 某一领域以美为主要标准
senses.definition: the tendency to put aesthetic appeal first in a domain outside art
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术之外的领域中把审美吸引力放在首位的倾向
senses.example: The brand's aestheticism puts beauty ahead of function.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌的唯美取向把美观放在功能之前。
senses.why: The doctrine's single criterion can be imported anywhere, so design, advertising or even engineering may be charged with aestheticism.
senses.whyCN: 这条主张的唯一标准可以被输入任何领域，因此设计、广告甚至工程都可能被指为唯美主义。

intro.en: Aestheticism is a nineteenth-century English formation: aesthetic plus -ism, recorded in 1855 and later tied to the art-for-art's-sake circle. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: aestheticism 是 19 世纪英语构词：aesthetic 加 -ism，1855 年有记录，后来与「为艺术而艺术」的圈子联系在一起。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aisthēsis 'perception' supplied the root of aesthetic; the sensory meaning is older than the meaning 'beautiful'.
items.cn: aisthēsis「感知」提供 aesthetic 的词根；感官义比「美」义更早。

items.en: Baumgarten's eighteenth-century coinage made aesthetics a name for the science of sensory knowledge.
items.cn: 鲍姆加登 18 世纪的造词使 aesthetics 成为感官知识之学的名称。

items.en: English aesthetic appeared in 1798; by the 1830s it commonly meant the appreciation of beauty.
items.cn: 英语 aesthetic 于 1798 年出现；到 1830 年代，它通常指对美的欣赏。

items.en: The suffix -ism, from Greek -ismos through Latin -ismus, names a practice, doctrine or movement.
items.cn: 后缀 -ism 经拉丁 -ismus 来自希腊 -ismos，命名一种实践、主张或运动。

items.en: Aestheticism is recorded in 1855 in the sense 'devotion to what is sensuously beautiful'.
items.cn: aestheticism 于 1855 年有记录，意为「对感官之美的献身」。

items.en: Later in the century the word was attached to Pater, Wilde and the art-for-art's-sake programme, and that historical sense now leads.
items.cn: 到该世纪后期，这个词与佩特、王尔德及「为艺术而艺术」纲领联系在一起，这一历史义如今最突出。

note.en: Group one separates aestheticism from the aisth- words it is built on; group two separates it from neighbouring movements and doctrines of art.
note.cn: 第一组把 aestheticism 与它所由来的 aisth- 词分开；第二组把它与邻近的艺术运动与主张分开。

entries.definition: A quality or principle of beauty; aestheticism is the doctrine that makes beauty supreme.
entries.definitionCN: 美的性质或原则；aestheticism 是把美置于至高位置的主张。

entries.definition: The philosophical study of beauty and art; it can analyse aestheticism without adopting it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究美与艺术的哲学；它可以分析唯美主义而不采纳它。

entries.definition: A devotee of beauty; aestheticism is the creed such a person may hold.
entries.definitionCN: 美的崇拜者；aestheticism 是此人可能持有的信条。

entries.definition: Loss of sensation; it shares the perceptual root but has no connection with the art movement.
entries.definitionCN: 感觉丧失；同出感知词根，但与这场艺术运动无关。

entries.definition: The French-derived phrase l'art pour l'art, translated in 1824; it is the slogan of aestheticism rather than its name.
entries.definitionCN: 源自法语 l'art pour l'art，1824 年有英译；它是唯美主义的口号，而不是其名称。

entries.definition: A late nineteenth-century literary mood of refinement and decline; it overlaps with aestheticism but adds exhaustion and perversity.
entries.definitionCN: 19 世纪后期的文学情绪，讲究精致与衰颓；与唯美主义重叠，但多了疲惫与乖僻。

entries.definition: The critical priority of formal structure over content; aestheticism is broader and adds a doctrine about beauty's value.
entries.definitionCN: 批评上把形式结构置于内容之上；aestheticism 更广，并附加关于美之价值的主张。

entries.definition: The cultivation of an elegant, conspicuous self-presentation; it is a social cousin of aestheticism, not the same programme.
entries.definitionCN: 对优雅而惹眼的自我呈现的经营；是唯美主义的社会近亲，而非同一纲领。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: aesthetic + -ism: the doctrine that beauty is the point.
normal.cn: aesthetic + -ism：以美为要旨的主张。

normal.en: -ism names movements as well as beliefs, so the word covers both a creed and a circle.
normal.cn: -ism 既命名主张也命名运动，因此这个词既指信条也指圈子。

normal.en: Fixed phrases date it: Victorian aestheticism, the aestheticism of the eighteen-nineties.
normal.cn: 固定搭配为它标年代：维多利亚唯美主义、19 世纪 90 年代的唯美主义。

normal.en: The family runs aesthetic, aesthetics, aesthete, aestheticism and aestheticist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 aesthetic、aesthetics、aesthete、aestheticism 与 aestheticist。

normal.en: The slogan art for art's sake translates French l'art pour l'art, recorded in English in 1824.
normal.cn: 口号「为艺术而艺术」译自法语 l'art pour l'art，英语 1824 年有记录。

abstract.en: Picture a room with every useful object removed and only colour left.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，实用物件全被移走，只剩下颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a frame that refuses to hold anything but the surface it shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个画框，只肯装它展示的那层表面。

abstract.en: Picture a life arranged with the same care as a shelf of porcelain.
abstract.cn: 想象一段生活被安排得像一柜瓷器那样精心。

examples.en: Aestheticism is often taught through the trial of Oscar Wilde.
examples.cn: 唯美主义常通过王尔德的审判来讲授。

examples.en: The movement's aestheticism did not deny politics; it refused to let politics judge art.
examples.cn: 这场运动的唯美主义并不否认政治，而是拒绝让政治评判艺术。

examples.en: Modern branding repeats the aestheticism of the eighteen-nineties in a commercial key.
examples.cn: 现代品牌以商业调子重复着 19 世纪 90 年代的唯美主义。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「aesthetic（审美的）+ -ism（主义）」——审美至上主义 → 唯美主义

root: aesthetic 来自希腊 aisthētikos「可感知的」，词根 aisthēsis「感知」；-ism 经拉丁 -ismus 来自希腊 -ismos，命名主张或运动。aestheticism 于 1855 年出现。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the historical movement to its doctrine, then to a personal creed, a way of life, a decorative style, a pejorative label, a critical method and finally a general criterion outside art.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从历史运动转到其主张，再到个人信条、生活方式、装饰风格、贬义标签、批评方法，最后落到艺术之外的普遍标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room emptied of useful things, where only colour and line remain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间移走实用物件、只留下颜色与线条的房间。

branches.en: THE MOVEMENT AND ITS CRITERION: a historical circle, then the same priority applied anywhere.
branches.cn: 运动及其标准：先是一个历史圈子，再是同一优先性被用到任何领域。

branches.en: THE DOCTRINE AND THE METHOD: art owes no moral lesson, and criticism reads for form.
branches.cn: 主张与方法：艺术不欠道德教训，批评则为形式而读。

branches.en: A CREED LIVED: devotion to beauty becomes a way of composing experience.
branches.cn: 被实践的信条：对美的献身变成安排经验的方式。

branches.en: A STYLE LEFT BEHIND: the movement survives in palettes, patterns and interiors.
branches.cn: 留下的风格：运动在色彩、纹样与室内中继续存在。

branches.en: THE MOCKING NAME: concern with surface becomes a charge of evasion.
branches.cn: 被讥讽之名：对表面的关注被指控为逃避。

intro.en: Aestheticism is a Greek root plus two suffixes, one making an adjective and one making a doctrine, so the whole word can be read in layers.
intro.cn: aestheticism 是希腊词根加两个后缀，一个构成形容词，一个构成主张，因此整个词可以分层读出。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek, not Latin; Latin contributes only the shape of the suffix -ismus, which English took through French -isme.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是希腊语而非拉丁语；拉丁语只提供后缀 -ismus 的形状，英语经法语 -isme 取得。

items.example: The root begins the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根开启整个词族。

items.example: The suffix makes aesthetic an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀使 aesthetic 成为形容词。

items.example: The aesthetic argument came first.
items.exampleCN: 审美论证先出现。

items.example: Realism and formalism use the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: realism 与 formalism 用的是同一个后缀。

items.meaning: the doctrine of beauty for its own sake
items.example: Aestheticism rejected moral instruction.
items.exampleCN: 唯美主义拒绝道德训诫。

items.example: The aestheticist wrote only about surfaces.
items.exampleCN: 这位唯美主义者只写表面。

items.example: The film aestheticizes the factory.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片把工厂审美化了。

items.meaning: from an aesthetic point of view
items.example: The street is aesthetically coherent.
items.exampleCN: 这条街在审美上是一致的。

items.example: Aesthetics can study aestheticism coldly.
items.exampleCN: 美学可以冷静地研究唯美主义。

definition_en: the quality of being pleasing to the senses or mind, or a person or thing that has this quality
core_image: 一张脸、一片山脊或一道证明，在被人看见的瞬间让呼吸慢了一拍
scene: 数学教室里，老师在黑板上写下一个很短的证明，学生安静下来。The class fell silent at the beauty of the short proof.
sceneCN: 这里 beauty 指「简洁优雅、令人赞叹的品质」（第 5 个义项：证明或解答的精妙之美）；句意为学生被这个简短证明的精妙震住而安静下来。

pos.zh: 美；美丽；美人；美的事物；妙处

derivatives.zh: beauty + -ful（充满）→ 美的；从「抽象品质」转到「具有该品质」
beautiful + -ly（副词）→ 美丽地；从「性质」转到「方式」
beauty + -ify（使……化）→ 使变美；从「状态」转到「施加动作」
beauty + -ician（从业者）→ 美容师；从「美」转到「以美为业的人」
beauty + -ous（充满）→ 有美感的；语义偏诗体，使用范围窄

senses.title: The quality of being beautiful
senses.definition: the quality that pleases the senses or the mind
senses.definitionCN: 使感官或心灵感到愉悦的品质
senses.example: The beauty of the valley stopped the walkers in their tracks.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷之美让步行者停下脚步。
senses.why: This is the abstract noun behind the adjective beautiful: the word names the quality itself, apart from any one object that has it.
senses.whyCN: 这是形容词 beautiful 背后的抽象名词：词命名品质本身，而不指某一具体拥有该品质的物件。

senses.title: A beautiful person
senses.definition: a beautiful person, especially a woman
senses.definitionCN: 美丽的人，尤指女性
senses.example: The portrait was praised as a great beauty of the age.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅肖像被赞为那个时代的大美人。
senses.why: Concrete for abstract: the quality stands for the person who possesses it, a standard metonymy that turns 'beauty' into 'a beauty'.
senses.whyCN: 以抽象代具体：品质代替拥有该品质的人，这是把「美」变成「一位美人」的标准转喻。

senses.title: A beautiful thing or feature
senses.definition: a beautiful thing, especially a feature of a place or work
senses.definitionCN: 美好的事物，尤指某地或某作品的动人之处
senses.example: We spent the afternoon listing the beauties of the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 我们花了一个下午列举老城的各处美景。
senses.why: The countable plural gathers particular instances of the quality, so a town can be praised by counting its beauties one by one.
senses.whyCN: 可数复数收集该品质的具体实例，因此可以一件件清点一座城镇的美来称赞它。

senses.title: Beauty of character
senses.definition: an inner quality of character that commands admiration
senses.definitionCN: 令人敬佩的内在品格
senses.example: Her beauty of character outlasted her looks.
senses.exampleCN: 她的品格之美比容貌更持久。
senses.why: The word moves from the senses to the mind: what pleases morally can be called beauty by a deliberate transfer of vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从感官转到心灵：在道德上令人愉悦之物，可以通过有意的词汇转移而被称为美。

senses.title: Elegance in a proof or solution
senses.definition: the economy and clarity that make an argument or solution admirable
senses.definitionCN: 使论证或解答令人赞叹的简洁与清晰
senses.example: The class fell silent at the beauty of the short proof.
senses.exampleCN: 学生被这个简短证明的精妙震住而安静下来。
senses.why: Mathematicians borrow the aesthetic word because a short proof can produce the same pleasure as a well-made form: nothing is wasted.
senses.whyCN: 数学家借用这个审美词，因为一个简短证明能带来与精良形式相同的愉悦：没有一处多余。

senses.title: The advantage of a plan
senses.definition: the particularly good or convenient feature of an arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 某项安排中特别好或方便的方面
senses.example: The beauty of the scheme is that it needs no new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案的好处在于不需要新增人员。
senses.why: From 'pleasing quality' comes 'pleasing feature': what makes a plan attractive is its beauty, even when nothing visual is involved.
senses.whyCN: 从「令人愉悦的品质」引申出「令人愉悦的方面」：使方案吸引人的地方就是它的 beauty，即使完全不涉及视觉。

senses.title: The appearance trade
senses.definition: the industry and practices devoted to enhancing physical appearance
senses.definitionCN: 致力于改善外貌的产业与实践
senses.example: The beauty industry spends millions on new promises.
senses.exampleCN: 美容产业花数百万制造新的承诺。
senses.why: An attributive use turns the quality into a market: beauty products, beauty salons and beauty work all sell the quality by name.
senses.whyCN: 定语用法把这种品质变成市场：美容产品、美容院与美容工作都直接以这种品质之名出售。

senses.title: An ideal of beauty in art
senses.definition: a shared standard or model of beauty, especially in a period or school
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期或流派共享的美的标准或典范
senses.example: The academy taught a classical ideal of beauty.
senses.exampleCN: 学院教授一种古典的美的理想。
senses.why: When a culture agrees on what counts as beautiful, the quality becomes a norm; art history calls that norm its ideal of beauty.
senses.whyCN: 当一个文化就何为美达成共识，这种品质就成了规范；艺术史把该规范称为它的美的理想。

intro.en: Beauty came into English in the early fourteenth century from Old French, ultimately from Latin bellus; the deeper origin of bellus is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: beauty 于 14 世纪初从古法语进入英语，最终来自拉丁 bellus；bellus 的更早来源没有定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Bellus meant 'pretty, handsome, charming', used especially of women and children and sometimes ironically of men; its earlier origin is uncertain, and the proposal that it is a diminutive of a root *deu- is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: bellus 意为「漂亮的、英俊的、迷人的」，多用于女性和儿童，有时反讽地用于男性；其更早来源不确定，认为它是 *deu- 词根指小形式的说法只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Vulgar Latin *bellitatem, nominative *bellitas, meant 'state of being pleasing to the senses'.
items.cn: 俗拉丁 *bellitatem（主格 *bellitas）意为「令感官愉悦的状态」。

items.en: Old French biauté or beauté (twelfth century) meant 'beauty, seductiveness, a beautiful person'.
items.cn: 古法语 biauté 或 beauté（12 世纪）意为「美、媚惑、美人」。

items.en: English bealte is recorded in the early fourteenth century for 'physical attractiveness', and also for 'goodness, courtesy'.
items.cn: 英语 bealte 于 14 世纪初有记录，指「外貌吸引力」，也指「善良、礼貌」。

items.en: Beauty replaced the native Old English word wlite, which had named splendour or appearance.
items.cn: beauty 取代了英语本族词 wlite，后者曾指光辉或外观。

items.en: From the seventeenth to the nineteenth century the word extended to inner beauty, the beauty of a proof or plan, and the beauty trade, each preserving the core idea of something that pleases.
items.cn: 从 17 到 19 世纪，这个词扩展到内在美、证明或方案的妙处以及美容产业，每一支都保留了「令人愉悦」这一核心。

note.en: Group one holds words built directly on beauty that are easy to confuse in form; group two holds nouns that also name an attractive quality but from narrower angles.
note.cn: 第一组是直接由 beauty 构成、形式上易混的词；第二组是同样命名吸引力、但角度更窄的名词。

entries.definition: Having beauty; the adjective describes the object, while beauty names the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 具有美的；形容词描述对象，beauty 则命名品质。

entries.definition: To make something beautiful; it names an action, not a state.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变美；命名动作，而非状态。

entries.definition: A poetic or archaic adjective for beautiful; modern prose usually prefers beautiful.
entries.definitionCN: 诗歌或古体的「美的」形容词；现代散文通常用 beautiful。

entries.definition: A person who provides cosmetic treatments; the ending marks a worker, not the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 提供美容护理的人；词尾标记从业者，而非品质。
