entries.definition: Beauty shown through simplicity and good proportion; it is narrower and often more formal than beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 通过简洁与良好比例显现的美；比 beauty 更窄，也往往更正式。

entries.definition: A quality that attracts or delights, often through personality rather than appearance.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引或取悦人的品质，常来自性格而非外貌。

entries.definition: A soft, endearing beauty; the word usually carries warmth and affection.
entries.definitionCN: 柔和可亲的美；通常带温暖与喜爱之情。

entries.definition: The power of drawing interest or desire; it can mean sexual appeal, which beauty need not.
entries.definitionCN: 引起兴趣或欲望的力量；可指性吸引力，而 beauty 未必含此义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The abstract noun stands behind beautiful, beautify and beautician.
normal.cn: 这个抽象名词支撑着 beautiful、beautify 与 beautician。

normal.en: Old French beauté and Latin bellus are the historical sources, not any English rhyme.
normal.cn: 历史来源是古法语 beauté 与拉丁 bellus，而不是任何英语顺口溜。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: natural beauty, inner beauty, the beauty of a plan.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：自然美、内在美、方案的妙处。

normal.en: The word replaced native wlite, which is why no modern relative of wlite survives in ordinary speech.
normal.cn: 这个词取代了本族词 wlite，因此日常语言中没有 wlite 的现代同族词。

normal.en: A mathematician's 'beautiful proof' is short: economy is part of the pleasure.
normal.cn: 数学家说的「漂亮的证明」往往很短：简洁本身就是愉悦的一部分。

abstract.en: Picture a breath that catches for a moment and then resumes.
abstract.cn: 想象一次短暂停顿又继续的呼吸。

abstract.en: Picture a standard held up in front of a face, measuring without touching.
abstract.cn: 想象一面举在脸前、只测量而不触碰的标尺。

abstract.en: Picture a quality that can move from a landscape to a line of argument.
abstract.cn: 想象一种能从风景迁移到论证的品质。

examples.en: The restoration recovered the beauty that the varnish had hidden.
examples.cn: 修复让被清漆遮住的美重新显露。

examples.en: He spoke of the beauty of the equation before explaining what it did.
examples.cn: 他先谈这个方程的美，再解释它的用途。

examples.en: Beauty standards change, but the pleasure of looking does not disappear.
examples.cn: 审美标准会变，但观看的愉悦不会消失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「beau（近似「波」）+ ty」——看一眼心里起波 → 美

root: 拉丁 bellus「漂亮的、迷人的」，经俗拉丁 *bellitas 与古法语 biauté、beauté 进入英语；bellus 更早来源不确定，指小词根的假说未获证实。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the abstract quality to a person, a place's features, character, a proof, a plan, a trade and finally a shared ideal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从抽象品质出发，转到人、景物、品格、证明、方案、产业，最后落到共享的理想。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face, a ridge or a proof makes the breath slow for a moment when it is seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张脸、一道山脊或一个证明，在被看见时让呼吸慢了一拍。

branches.en: THE QUALITY AND ITS NORM: what pleases, and the standard a culture sets for it.
branches.cn: 品质及其规范：令人愉悦之物，以及一个文化为此设定的标准。

branches.en: EMBODIED AND SOLD: a person, a place's features, and the trade that packages appearance.
branches.cn: 被具身与被出售：一个人、一地的景致，以及把外貌打包出售的产业。

branches.en: INWARD BEAUTY: the vocabulary of the senses is lent to character.
branches.cn: 内在美：感官的词汇被借给品格。

branches.en: ELEGANCE: nothing wasted, so a proof gives the same pleasure as a form.
branches.cn: 精妙：没有多余，因此证明给出与形式相同的愉悦。

branches.en: ADVANTAGE: a plan's good feature is its beauty in plain speech.
branches.cn: 妙处：方案的好处，在口语中就是它的美。

intro.en: Beauty is a Latin-derived noun whose family grows through English suffixes; the root is no longer productive on its own.
intro.cn: beauty 是拉丁来源的名词，其词族通过英语后缀扩展；这个词根本身已不再能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin bellus and its vulgar noun *bellitas are the source; the family in English is built on the French form, not directly on a living Latin verb.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是拉丁 bellus 及其俗拉丁名词 *bellitas；英语词族建立在法语形式上，而非直接建立在活的拉丁动词上。

items.structure: Old French beauté, from Latin bellus
items.example: Beauty is easier to point at than to define.
items.exampleCN: 美更容易被指出，而不容易被定义。

items.example: Beautiful adds the suffix to the noun.
items.exampleCN: beautiful 把后缀加在名词上。

items.example: A beautiful line can be very simple.
items.exampleCN: 一条美的线条可以非常简单。

items.example: The room was beautifully lit.
items.exampleCN: 房间的灯光很美。

items.example: She sang beautifully.
items.exampleCN: 她唱得很美。

items.example: Beautify turns the noun into a verb.
items.exampleCN: beautify 把名词变成动词。

items.example: They beautified the square with trees.
items.exampleCN: 他们用树木美化广场。

items.example: Beautician follows the pattern of musician.
items.exampleCN: beautician 沿用了 musician 的构词模式。

items.example: The beautician ran a small salon.
items.exampleCN: 这位美容师经营一家小店。

definition_zh: 视觉的；看得见的；图像的
definition_en: relating to sight or to things that are seen, especially images rather than words
core_image: 一束光落进眼睛，在脑中变成一张可以被指认的图
scene: 博物馆入口，新指示牌用大图标代替长句，观众一眼就找到展厅方向。The new signage relies on visual cues rather than long labels.
sceneCN: 这里 visual 指「以图像形式呈现、供眼睛识别的」（第 3 个义项：与图像而非文字有关的）；句意为新指示牌依靠视觉提示，而不是长段文字说明。

pos.zh: 视觉的；看得见的；图像的
视觉图像；（影视、演示中的）画面素材

derivatives.zh: visual + -ly（副词）→ 视觉上；从「感官」转到「方式」
visual + -ize（使……化）→ 使在心中成像；从「视觉」转到「心理动作」
visualize + -ation（动作或结果）→ 可视化；从「动作」转到「产物」
visual + -s（复数名词化）→ 画面素材；从「性质」转到「具体材料」
visual + -ity（名词后缀）→ 视觉性；从「视觉的」转到「可被观看的特质」

senses.title: Relating to the sense of sight
senses.definition: connected with the sense of sight or with seeing
senses.definitionCN: 与视觉或看见这一能力有关的
senses.example: Visual processing begins in the retina.
senses.exampleCN: 视觉处理从视网膜开始。
senses.why: The adjective is built on Latin visus 'sight', so its first job is to mark anything belonging to the eye's faculty.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由拉丁 visus「视觉」构成，因此首要功能是标记属于眼睛能力的事物。

senses.title: Able to be seen
senses.definition: visible; perceptible by the eye
senses.definitionCN: 可见的；眼睛能感知到的
senses.example: A visual signal warned ships away from the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 一个可见信号警示船只远离礁石。
senses.why: What belongs to sight can also be what sight can catch; the adjective shifts from the faculty to the object it registers.
senses.whyCN: 属于视觉的东西也可以是视觉能捕捉到的东西；形容词从能力转到它所记录的对象。

senses.title: Based on images rather than words
senses.titleCN: 以图像而非文字为主的
senses.definition: expressed through pictures, graphics or images rather than text
senses.definitionCN: 通过图画、图形或图像而非文字表达的
senses.example: The new signage relies on visual cues rather than long labels.
senses.exampleCN: 新指示牌依靠视觉提示，而不是长段文字说明。
senses.why: Modern media contrast the visual with the verbal, so the adjective comes to mean 'carried by images' in a world full of text.
senses.whyCN: 现代媒介把「视觉的」与「文字的」对立，因此这个词在满是文字的世界里获得「由图像承载」之义。

senses.title: A single image on screen
senses.definition: a particular image, shot or graphic shown on screen
senses.definitionCN: 屏幕上显示的一幅具体图像、镜头或图形
senses.example: The director cut from the crowd to a single visual of the empty street.
senses.exampleCN: 导演从人群切到空荡街道的一幅画面。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun by ellipsis: a visual image is shortened to a visual, and the count shifts from quality to object.
senses.whyCN: 形容词通过省略变成名词：visual image 被简称为 a visual，计数对象从性质转为物件。

senses.title: Graphic material as a set
senses.definition: the collection of images and graphics used in a presentation or campaign
senses.definitionCN: 演示或宣传中使用的图像与图形总称
senses.example: The campaign's visuals were shot in one afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 这场宣传的整套画面素材在一个下午拍完。
senses.why: The plural gathers many single images into a working set, the way 'effects' gathers many tricks.
senses.whyCN: 复数把许多单幅图像收成一个工作套件，正如 effects 收拢许多特效。

senses.title: A teaching aid for the eye
senses.titleCN: 供眼睛使用的教学辅助
senses.definition: a picture, diagram or object used to support teaching
senses.definitionCN: 用于辅助教学的图画、图表或实物
senses.example: The teacher brought visuals for every new term.
senses.exampleCN: 老师为每个新术语都准备了视觉教具。
senses.why: Education borrowed the word for aids that make an idea visible, because seeing is treated as a shortcut to understanding.
senses.whyCN: 教育借用这个词指使概念可见的教具，因为看见被视为理解的捷径。

senses.title: Acuity or perception, in technical use
senses.titleCN: 技术用语中的视力或感知
senses.definition: the sharpness or functioning of sight, as in visual acuity
senses.definitionCN: 视觉的敏锐度或功能，如 visual acuity
senses.example: The test measures visual acuity at six metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测试测量六米距离处的视力。
senses.why: Clinical language fixes the adjective to measurable properties of seeing, so visual names the capacity's precision.
senses.whyCN: 临床语言把这个形容词固定到可测量的观看属性，因此 visual 命名该能力的精确度。

senses.title: Image output in technical use
senses.titleCN: 技术用语中的图像输出
senses.definition: the image or display produced by a device
senses.definitionCN: 设备产生的图像或显示结果
senses.example: Engineers checked the visual output before the launch.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在发布前检查了图像输出。
senses.why: Machines extend the sense from human sight to any image a screen can present, so output itself is called visual.
senses.whyCN: 机器把词义从人的视觉扩展到屏幕能呈现的任何图像，因此输出本身也被称为 visual。

intro.en: Visual comes from Late Latin visualis, built on Latin visus 'sight', the past participle of videre 'to see'; the English adjective is recorded from the early fifteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: visual 来自晚期拉丁 visualis，由拉丁 visus「视觉」构成，而 visus 是 videre「看见」的过去分词；英语形容词自 15 世纪初有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Videre meant 'to see'; its deeper root is reconstructed as PIE *weid- 'to see, know', the same root that gives video and evident.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」；其更早词根拟为印欧 *weid-「看见、知道」，同一词根也给出 video 与 evident。

items.en: Visus, the past participle of videre, meant 'a sight, a looking; the power of sight; things seen'.
items.cn: visus 是 videre 的过去分词，意为「看见、一次观看；视力；所见之物」。

items.en: Late Latin visualis meant 'of sight', formed from visus with the adjective suffix -alis.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 visualis 意为「视觉的」，由 visus 加形容词后缀 -alis 构成。

items.en: English visual is recorded in the early fifteenth century for 'pertaining to the faculty of sight'.
items.cn: 英语 visual 于 15 世纪初有记录，指「与视觉能力有关的」。

items.en: The noun use for a photographic image or display is recorded from 1944, when screens and film made 'a visual' countable.
items.cn: 指照片影像或显示画面的名词用法自 1944 年有记录，屏幕与胶片使「一幅画面」变得可数。

items.en: In the later twentieth century visuals became the standard term for the image material of a film, campaign or presentation.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪后期，visuals 成为电影、宣传或演示所用画面素材的标准说法。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same sight-root that look close but point to different things; group two holds adjectives that also concern pictures or seeing.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「看」词根、看似接近却指向不同事物的词；第二组是同样涉及图像或观看的形容词。

entries.definition: The faculty of sight, something seen, or an imagined future; visual is the adjective, vision the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 视力、所见之物或想象的未来；visual 是形容词，vision 是名词。

entries.definition: To form a mental image or make something visible; it names the act, not the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 在脑中成像或使某物可见；命名动作，而非性质。

entries.definition: A protective or projecting shield on a helmet; it comes through French vis 'face' from the same sight-root, but names an object.
entries.definitionCN: 头盔上的护面或帽檐；经法语 vis「脸」同出「看」词根，但命名物件。

entries.definition: Capable of being seen; visual can also mean 'relating to images', while visible only says it can be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 能被看见的；visual 还可指「与图像有关」，visible 只表示可见。

entries.definition: Relating to light, lenses or the physics of sight; visual is broader and includes images and media.
entries.definitionCN: 与光、透镜或视觉物理有关；visual 更广，包含图像与媒介。

entries.definition: Relating to drawing, design or printed pictures; visual may include photography and film.
entries.definitionCN: 与绘画、设计或印刷图形有关；visual 可包含摄影与电影。

entries.definition: Relating to pictures or painted images; it often describes a style rich in images.
entries.definitionCN: 与图画或绘画影像有关；常描述图像丰富的风格。

entries.definition: The ordinary past participle of see; visual is the technical or media adjective.
entries.definitionCN: see 的普通过去分词；visual 是技术或媒介用语中的形容词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin videre 'see' gives visus 'sight' and visualis 'of sight'.
normal.cn: 拉丁 videre「看见」给出 visus「视觉」与 visualis「视觉的」。

normal.en: The same root appears in video, evident and vision, all through the idea of seeing or knowing.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 video、evident 与 vision 中，都经由「看见或知道」这一观念。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the media sense: visual media, visual effects, visual identity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出媒介义：视觉媒介、视觉特效、视觉识别。

normal.en: The noun 'a visual' is simply a shortened visual image.
normal.cn: 名词 a visual 只是 visual image 的省略。

normal.en: The family runs visual, visually, visualize, visualization and visuals.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 visual、visually、visualize、visualization 与 visuals。

abstract.en: Picture light entering an eye and leaving as a shape the mind can name.
abstract.cn: 想象光进入眼睛，出来时变成心灵能命名的形状。

abstract.en: Picture a sign that needs no sentence to be understood.
abstract.cn: 想象一个不需要句子就能被理解的标识。

abstract.en: Picture a screen that keeps a copy of what the eye just did.
abstract.cn: 想象一块屏幕保存下眼睛刚完成的那件事。

examples.en: Visual memory holds the shape of a room long after the words are forgotten.
examples.cn: 文字早已忘记，视觉记忆却仍留着房间的形状。

examples.en: The report pairs visual evidence with a short written account.
examples.cn: 报告把视觉证据与简短文字说明配在一起。

examples.en: Her visual style is recognisable from a single frame.
examples.cn: 她的视觉风格从一个画面就能辨认。

root: 拉丁 videre「看见」的过去分词 visus「视觉」，加后缀 -alis 成晚期拉丁 visualis；更早词根拟为印欧 *weid-「看见、知道」，属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the faculty of sight to what can be seen, then to images as a medium, a single picture, a set of pictures, a teaching aid, measured acuity and machine output.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从视觉能力转到可见之物，再到作为媒介的图像、单幅画面、整套素材、教学辅助、测量视力与机器输出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: light falls into an eye and becomes a picture the mind can point to.
core.cn: 核心意象：光落进眼睛，变成心灵能够指认的一幅图。

branches.en: SIGHT AND ITS SHARPNESS: the faculty itself, then its measured precision.
branches.cn: 视觉及其锐度：能力本身，然后是它被测量的精确度。

branches.en: WHAT CAN BE CAUGHT: the object that the faculty registers.
branches.cn: 可被捕捉之物：能力所记录的对象。

branches.en: IMAGE AS MEDIUM: pictures carry meaning, and pictures assist teaching.
branches.cn: 作为媒介的图像：图像承载意义，也辅助教学。

branches.en: ONE AND MANY: a single screen image, then the whole working set.
branches.cn: 一与多：一幅屏幕画面，然后是整套工作素材。

branches.en: MACHINE OUTPUT: the image a device produces, seen without a human eye.
branches.cn: 机器输出：设备产生的图像，不依赖人眼也在那里。

intro.en: Visual is a Latin participle stem plus a Latin adjective suffix, and the stem also builds the noun for sight and the verb for making images.
intro.cn: visual 是拉丁分词词干加拉丁形容词后缀，同一词干还构成表示视力的名词与表示成像的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre 'to see' has the participle visus; Late Latin added -alis. The same family yields vision, video and evident.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 videre「看见」有分词 visus；晚期拉丁再加 -alis。同一词族给出 vision、video 与 evident。

items.example: The root underlies video and evident.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根支撑着 video 与 evident。

items.example: Visus supplies the stem of visual.
items.exampleCN: visus 提供 visual 的词干。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun of sight into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「视觉」名词变成形容词。

items.example: The visual field is wider than the sharp centre.
items.exampleCN: 视野比清晰的中心区域更宽。

items.example: The two panels are visually paired.
items.exampleCN: 两块面板在视觉上成对。

items.example: He visualized the finished room.
items.exampleCN: 他在脑中想象出完工的房间。

items.meaning: the act or product of imaging
items.example: The chart is a visualization of the data.
items.exampleCN: 这张图是数据的可视化。

items.meaning: sight; a thing seen; an imagined future
items.meaningCN: 视力；所见之物；想象的远景
items.example: The plan began as a vision.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划始于一个愿景。

items.example: Video keeps what the eye saw.
items.exampleCN: 视频保存下眼睛所见。

latinEntries.meaning: the act of seeing; a thing seen

definition_zh: 视觉艺术；造型艺术（绘画、雕塑、摄影、设计等）
definition_en: art forms that are primarily seen, such as painting, drawing, sculpture, photography and design
core_image: 一排作品挂在墙上，观众只能靠眼睛进入它们
scene: 展厅把架上绘画与声音装置放进同一空间，逼观众思考界线在哪里。The exhibition sets visual art beside a sound installation to test where the boundary lies.
sceneCN: 这里 visual art 指「以视觉为媒介的整个艺术类别」（第 1 个义项：统称绘画、雕塑、摄影等门类）；句意为展览把视觉艺术与声音装置并置，测试两者界线。

pos.zh: 视觉艺术（总称，通常不可数；可数时指一件作品或一个门类）

collocations.zh: 视觉艺术（总称，常用复数）

derivatives.zh: visual art + -ist（人）→ 视觉艺术家；从「类别」转到「从业者」
visual art + -s（复数类别）→ 视觉艺术总称；从「一门」转到「多门类集合」
visual artist + -s（复数）→ 视觉艺术家们；仅数量变化
visual art + -ry（技艺、实践）→ 视觉艺术技巧；从「门类」转到「实践功夫」

senses.title: The umbrella category
senses.definition: the category of art forms addressed primarily to the eye
senses.definitionCN: 主要以眼睛为对象的艺术门类总称
senses.example: The exhibition sets visual art beside a sound installation.
senses.exampleCN: 展览把视觉艺术与声音装置并置。
senses.why: The phrase names a category by its channel: art that reaches the viewer through sight rather than sound, text or performance.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语按接收通道命名类别：通过视觉而非声音、文字或表演抵达观众的艺术。

senses.title: A particular work in these forms
senses.definition: one work belonging to the visual arts
senses.definitionCN: 属于视觉艺术门类的一件作品
senses.example: The museum acquired a major visual art from the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆从遗产中购得一件重要的视觉艺术作品。
senses.why: A category name can be used countably for its members, so one painting or photograph can be called a visual art.
senses.whyCN: 类别名称可以可数地用于其成员，因此一幅画或一张照片可以被称为 a visual art。

senses.title: The practice of making it
senses.definition: the activity or practice of making visual art
senses.definitionCN: 创作视觉艺术的活动或实践
senses.example: She works in visual art rather than in theatre.
senses.exampleCN: 她从事视觉艺术，而不是戏剧。
senses.why: The name of a product category also names the labour that produces it, as with 'painting' and 'sculpture'.
senses.whyCN: 产品类别的名称也命名生产它的劳动，正如 painting 与 sculpture 那样。

senses.title: The field as a profession
senses.titleCN: 作为职业领域的视觉艺术
senses.definition: the professional world of galleries, commissions and funding for visual art
senses.definitionCN: 由画廊、委托与资助构成的视觉艺术职业世界
senses.example: She has worked in visual art for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在视觉艺术行业工作了二十年。
senses.why: An art world is a set of institutions, so the phrase can name the field as a career rather than a medium.
senses.whyCN: 艺术世界是一组机构，因此这个短语能指作为职业的领域，而非媒介。

senses.title: A school subject
senses.titleCN: 学校课程中的视觉艺术
senses.definition: the subject taught in schools under this name
senses.definitionCN: 学校以该名称教授的科目
senses.example: Visual art is timetabled twice a week.
senses.exampleCN: 视觉艺术每周排两次课。
senses.why: Curricula turn fields into subjects, so the phrase can mean the classroom slot rather than the whole art world.
senses.whyCN: 课程表把领域变成科目，因此这个短语能指课堂位置，而非整个艺术界。

senses.title: The contrast with performing arts
senses.titleCN: 与表演艺术相对的门类
senses.definition: the category defined by contrast with music, dance and theatre
senses.definitionCN: 通过与音乐、舞蹈、戏剧对照而界定的类别
senses.example: Funding divides visual art from performing art.
senses.exampleCN: 资助体系把视觉艺术与表演艺术分开。
senses.why: Categories are often made by contrast: what is not performed live for an audience is grouped as visual.
senses.whyCN: 类别常通过对照建立：不在现场为观众表演的，就被归为视觉艺术。

senses.title: A market category
senses.definition: the grouping used by dealers, auctions and collectors
senses.definitionCN: 画商、拍卖与收藏界使用的分类
senses.example: Visual art sales rose while print sales fell.
senses.exampleCN: 视觉艺术销售额上升，版画销售额下降。
senses.why: Markets need sortable labels, so the phrase becomes a sales category covering objects that can be owned and hung.
senses.whyCN: 市场需要可分类的标签，因此这个短语成为销售类别，涵盖可以拥有与悬挂的物件。

senses.title: An academic field
senses.definition: the field of study and degree programmes devoted to visual art
senses.definitionCN: 以视觉艺术为对象的研究领域与学位项目
senses.example: The university offers a degree in visual art.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学提供视觉艺术学位。
senses.why: When a practice enters universities, its name also names the department and the degree, a familiar institutional shift.
senses.whyCN: 当一种实践进入大学，其名称也命名院系与学位，这是常见的机构化转移。

intro.en: Visual art joins a Late Latin adjective of sight to a Latin noun for skill; the compound is modern, though both parts are old. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: visual art 把晚期拉丁的「视觉」形容词与拉丁的「技艺」名词结合；两部分都古老，复合词却是现代产物。年代均为约数。

items.en: Videre 'to see' gives the participle visus and the Late Latin adjective visualis 'of sight'.
items.cn: videre「看见」给出分词 visus 与晚期拉丁形容词 visualis「视觉的」。

items.en: Ars, artis meant practical skill or craft; the modern category of the fine arts grew from this word in the Renaissance and after.
items.cn: ars、artis 意为实用技艺或手艺；现代「美术」类别在文艺复兴及以后从这个词生长出来。

items.en: English art is recorded from the thirteenth century and visual from the fifteenth; the two words long led separate lives.
items.cn: 英语 art 自 13 世纪有记录，visual 自 15 世纪有记录；两词长期各自发展。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries museums, schools and funding agencies grouped painting, sculpture, printmaking, photography and design as the visual arts.
items.cn: 到 19 与 20 世纪，博物馆、学校与资助机构把绘画、雕塑、版画、摄影与设计归为视觉艺术。

items.en: The plural visual arts became standard in arts education and public funding, and the singular visual art followed as a subject name.
items.cn: 复数 visual arts 在艺术教育与公共资助中成为标准说法，单数 visual art 随后成为科目名称。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the compound has no agreed first citation, and its boundary with fine art or design is still argued.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个复合词没有公认的最早书证，它与美术或设计的界线至今仍有争论。

note.en: Group one separates the singular, plural and personal forms that are often mixed up; group two separates visual art from categories that overlap but answer a different question.
note.cn: 第一组把常被混用的单数、复数与指人形式分开；第二组把视觉艺术与有重叠但回答不同问题的类别分开。

entries.definition: The standard collective name for the group of disciplines; the singular often names a subject or one work.
entries.definitionCN: 该组门类的标准总称；单数常指一个科目或一件作品。

entries.definition: A practitioner in the visual arts; the phrase names a person, not a category.
entries.definitionCN: 视觉艺术的从业者；这个短语指人，而非类别。

entries.definition: The study of all visual media, including advertising and scientific images; visual art keeps the art category.
entries.definitionCN: 研究一切视觉媒介，包括广告与科学图像；visual art 保留艺术类别。

entries.definition: The arrangement of graphics for communication; it may be taught beside visual art but serves a client's purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为传达而安排图形；可能与视觉艺术同教，但服务客户目的。

entries.definition: Art valued for beauty and expression, especially painting and sculpture; visual art is the wider, medium-based category.
entries.definitionCN: 因美与表达而被珍视的艺术，尤指绘画与雕塑；visual art 是更广的、按媒介划分的类别。

entries.definition: Arts that shape material into three-dimensional form, such as sculpture and ceramics; visual art also covers flat images.
entries.definitionCN: 把材料塑成立体形式的艺术，如雕塑与陶艺；visual art 也包含平面图像。

entries.definition: Art made for a practical function, such as furniture or typography; visual art does not decide by function.
entries.definitionCN: 为实用功能而作的艺术，如家具或字体设计；visual art 不以功能来划分。

entries.definition: Art presented live before an audience, such as dance or theatre; it is the usual contrast term.
entries.definitionCN: 在观众面前现场呈现的艺术，如舞蹈或戏剧；是常用的对照词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: visual + art: art that reaches you through the eye.
normal.cn: visual + art：通过眼睛抵达你的艺术。

normal.en: The plural visual arts is the standard collective name in schools and funding.
normal.cn: 复数 visual arts 是学校与资助体系中的标准总称。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: visual art practice, visual art education, a degree in visual art.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：视觉艺术实践、视觉艺术教育、视觉艺术学位。

normal.en: The family runs visual, visual arts, visual artist and visual culture.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 visual、visual arts、visual artist 与 visual culture。

normal.en: The category is defined by contrast with performing art, not by one medium.
normal.cn: 这个类别靠与表演艺术对照来界定，而不是靠单一媒介。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that lets only eyes through.
abstract.cn: 想象一面只放眼睛通过的墙。

abstract.en: Picture a room where sound is the exception and sight the rule.
abstract.cn: 想象一个以视觉为常规、声音为例外的房间。

abstract.en: Picture a label broad enough to hold a drawing, a photograph and a building.
abstract.cn: 想象一个宽到能装下素描、照片与建筑的标签。

examples.en: Visual art and music share a gallery but not a budget line.
examples.cn: 视觉艺术与音乐共用展厅，却不在同一预算科目下。

examples.en: The course treats visual art as a way of thinking, not only of making.
examples.cn: 这门课把视觉艺术当作一种思考方式，而不只是制作方式。

examples.en: Photography's place in visual art was settled only in the twentieth century.
examples.cn: 摄影在视觉艺术中的位置到 20 世纪才被确定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「visual（视觉的）+ art（艺术）」——给眼睛看的艺术 → 视觉艺术

root: visual 来自拉丁 videre「看见」的分词 visus 与晚期拉丁 visualis；art 来自拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺」。二者合成现代英语复合词 visual art，19 至 20 世纪成为机构类别。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses distinguish the category from one work, the practice, the profession, the school subject, the contrast with performance, the market and the academic field.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把类别与单件作品、创作实践、职业、学校科目、与表演的对照、市场及学术领域区分开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of works hangs on a wall, and viewers can enter them only through the eye.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排作品挂在墙上，观众只能靠眼睛进入它们。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY AND ITS EDGE: the umbrella term, then the contrast that defines it.
branches.cn: 类别及其边界：总称，然后是界定它的对照。

branches.en: ONE WORK: the category used countably for a single piece.
branches.cn: 单件作品：类别被可数地用于一件作品。

branches.en: THE PRACTICE: the labour behind the category.
branches.cn: 实践：类别背后的劳动。

branches.en: PROFESSION AND MARKET: the field as a career, then as a sales category.
branches.cn: 职业与市场：领域作为职业，再作为销售类别。

branches.en: SCHOOL AND UNIVERSITY: the subject in a timetable, then the degree and department.
branches.cn: 中小学与大学：课表上的科目，再是学位与院系。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived adjective of sight to a Latin-derived noun of skill, and each half keeps its own family.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源的「视觉」形容词与拉丁来源的「技艺」名词结合，两半各保留自己的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre supplies visual through visus and visualis; Latin ars supplies art. The compound itself is modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 videre 经 visus 与 visualis 提供 visual；拉丁 ars 提供 art。复合词本身是现代英语的产物。

items.example: Visual marks the channel.
items.exampleCN: visual 标记接收通道。

items.example: Art marks the category.
items.exampleCN: art 标记类别。

items.example: The museum collects visual art of the last century.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆收藏上一个世纪的视觉艺术。

items.meaningCN: 各视觉艺术门类的总称
items.example: The faculty of visual arts has four departments.
items.exampleCN: 视觉艺术学院有四个系。

items.meaning: a maker in the visual arts
items.example: The visual artist works in video and clay.
items.exampleCN: 这位视觉艺术家用录像与黏土创作。

items.example: The artist signed the print.
items.exampleCN: 艺术家在版画上签了名。

items.example: The suffix turns a field into a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把领域变成人。

items.example: The software visualizes the plan.
items.exampleCN: 这款软件把方案可视化。

definition_zh: 美术（尤指绘画、雕塑、建筑等）；高雅艺术；精湛技艺
definition_en: art valued for beauty and expression rather than practical use, especially painting, sculpture and architecture
core_image: 一件不拿来用的东西被放在台座上，只为让人看
scene: 谈判桌上，老练的中间人先让对方把底线说出来，再慢慢回应。The mediator practised the fine art of letting the other side speak first.
sceneCN: 这里 fine art 用于固定说法「the fine art of...」，指「需要高超技巧与分寸的技艺」（第 8 个义项：某种精细的处事本领）；句意为调停者运用「先让对方开口」这门精细手艺。

pos.zh: 美术；高雅艺术（通常不可数）；the fine art of... 指精湛技艺

derivatives.zh: fine art + -s（复数）→ 各门美术；从「类别」转到「多门学科集合」
fine art + -ist（从业者）→ 美术家；从「领域」转到「人」
fine artist + -s（复数）→ 美术家们；仅数量变化

senses.title: Art valued for beauty, not use
senses.titleCN: 以美与表达为目的而非实用的艺术
senses.definition: art made chiefly to be beautiful or expressive rather than useful
senses.definitionCN: 主要为美或表达而创作、而非为实用的艺术
senses.example: The museum separates fine art from design.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把美术与设计分开。
senses.why: Fine here carries its old sense of 'of the highest quality', and art carries 'skill'; together they name work whose end is aesthetic rather than practical.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 fine 保留旧义「最高品质」，art 保留「技艺」；合起来命名以审美而非实用为目的的作品。

senses.title: The fine arts as a group
senses.definition: the group of disciplines traditionally including painting, sculpture and architecture
senses.definitionCN: 传统上包括绘画、雕塑与建筑的一组学科
senses.example: The academy teaches the fine arts as separate departments.
senses.exampleCN: 学院把各门美术分成独立系科教授。
senses.why: The plural turns the category into a list: each medium becomes a discipline, and the phrase names them together.
senses.whyCN: 复数把类别变成清单：每种媒介成为一门学科，短语把它们合称。

senses.title: A particular work of fine art
senses.definition: one work belonging to the fine arts
senses.definitionCN: 属于美术门类的一件作品
senses.example: The auction offered a fine-art piece by a living sculptor.
senses.exampleCN: 拍卖会推出一件在世雕塑家的美术作品。
senses.why: Category names can be used for members, especially in attributive form, so a single object can be marked as belonging to fine art.
senses.whyCN: 类别名称可用于成员，尤其在定语形式中，因此单件物品可以被标记为属于美术。

senses.title: The border with craft
senses.definition: the category defined against craft and applied art
senses.definitionCN: 通过与工艺、应用艺术对照而界定的类别
senses.example: The show blurs the line between fine art and craft.
senses.exampleCN: 这场展览模糊了美术与工艺的界线。
senses.why: A category needs an outside: fine art is what claims beauty before function, while craft is judged by use and technique.
senses.whyCN: 类别需要一个外部：美术声称美先于功能，而工艺按用途与技术来评判。

senses.title: The market and collecting
senses.definition: the commercial field of dealers, auctions and collectors in fine art
senses.definitionCN: 画商、拍卖与收藏者构成的美术商业领域
senses.example: Fine art sales outperformed the wider market.
senses.exampleCN: 美术品销售表现优于整体市场。
senses.why: Unique objects need a market of their own, so the category name becomes a trade label for authenticated originals.
senses.whyCN: 独一无二的物件需要自己的市场，因此类别名称成为经认证原作的交易标签。

senses.title: Photography's contested place
senses.definition: the debated inclusion of photography within fine art
senses.definitionCN: 摄影是否属于美术的争论
senses.example: Photography fought for a place in fine art for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影为进入美术之列争取了一个世纪。
senses.why: A reproductive medium challenged the category's claim to unique handmade beauty, so the phrase became the prize in that argument.
senses.whyCN: 可复制的媒介挑战了该类别对独一无二手作之美的声称，因此这个短语成了争论的奖品。

senses.title: Training and the academy
senses.definition: the academic training and institutions devoted to fine art
senses.definitionCN: 专攻美术的学院训练与机构
senses.example: She studied fine art before turning to set design.
senses.exampleCN: 她先学美术，后来转向舞台设计。
senses.why: Academies turned the category into a curriculum, so the phrase also names the degree and the studio training.
senses.whyCN: 学院把类别变成课程，因此这个短语也命名学位与工作室训练。

senses.title: The 'fine art of' doing something
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase the fine art of, a skill requiring delicacy and judgement
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法 the fine art of 中，指需要细腻与判断力的技艺
senses.example: The mediator practised the fine art of letting the other side speak first.
senses.exampleCN: 调停者运用「先让对方开口」这门精细手艺。
senses.why: The phrase borrows the prestige of fine art for ordinary skills: anything done with delicacy can be dressed as an art, and 'fine' adds the note of refinement.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法把美术的声望借给日常技能：任何做得细腻的事都能被包装成一门艺术，而 fine 加上「精细」的意味。

intro.en: Fine art is an eighteenth-century English phrase translating French beaux-arts; fine goes back through Old French to Latin finis, and art to Latin ars. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fine art 是 18 世纪英语短语，译自法语 beaux-arts；fine 经古法语上溯拉丁 finis，art 上溯拉丁 ars。年代均为约数。

items.en: Finis meant 'end, boundary'; Old French fin developed the sense 'perfected, of the highest quality', generally explained by the notion of the end or peak of a scale.
items.cn: finis 意为「终点、边界」；古法语 fin 发展出「精炼的、最高品质的」之义，通常用「量程的终点或顶点」来解释。

items.en: Ars, artis meant practical skill or craft, and by the Renaissance it also named the liberal and visual arts.
items.cn: ars、artis 意为实用技艺或手艺，到文艺复兴也用来指自由艺术与视觉艺术。

items.en: French beaux-arts, literally 'beautiful arts', named the arts of beauty in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
items.cn: 法语 beaux-arts 字面为「美的艺术」，在 17 与 18 世纪指以美为目标的艺术。

items.en: English fine art is recorded around 1760 as a translation of beaux-arts, at first in the singular as a category name.
items.cn: 英语 fine art 约 1760 年有记录，是 beaux-arts 的翻译，最初以单数作类别名。

items.en: Nineteenth-century art schools and exhibitions separated fine art from applied art and craft, fixing the modern contrast.
items.cn: 19 世纪的艺术学校与展览把美术与应用艺术、工艺分开，确立了现代对照。

items.en: Twentieth-century auction houses and galleries made fine art a market category for unique, authenticated works.
items.cn: 20 世纪的拍卖行与画廊使美术成为独一无二、经认证作品的交易类别。

note.en: Group one separates the phrase from forms that look almost identical; group two separates it from categories that overlap but judge by a different standard.
note.cn: 第一组把该短语与几乎同形的形式分开；第二组把它与有重叠、但按不同标准评判的类别分开。

entries.definition: The several disciplines taken together, especially in a faculty or degree title; fine art can name the category as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 各门学科合称，尤用于学院或学位名称；fine art 可指整体类别。

entries.definition: The French phrase from which fine art translates; in English it often appears in institutional names.
entries.definitionCN: fine art 所译的法语短语；在英语中常出现在机构名称里。

entries.definition: On its own fine means excellent, thin or delicate; only in the phrase does it mark the category of beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时意为优良、纤细或精细；只有在这个短语里才标记美的类别。

entries.definition: A practitioner of fine art, as opposed to a commercial or applied artist.
entries.definitionCN: 美术从业者，相对于商业或应用艺术家。

entries.definition: Art considered serious and culturally elevated; the label is social, while fine art is categorical.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为严肃而有文化高度的艺术；这个标签是社会性的，而 fine art 是类别性的。

entries.definition: Art addressed to the eye, including photography and design; fine art decides by beauty rather than by sense.
entries.definitionCN: 以眼睛为对象的艺术，包括摄影与设计；fine art 按美而非按感官划分。

entries.definition: Art made to serve a practical function; it is the usual opposite of fine art.
entries.definitionCN: 为实用功能而作的艺术；是 fine art 的常用反义类别。

entries.definition: Making by hand with trained skill, often useful; fine art claims aesthetic value beyond technique.
entries.definitionCN: 以训练有素的技艺手工制作，常具实用性；fine art 声称技法之外还有审美价值。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: fine (of the highest quality) + art: art at the top of the scale.
normal.cn: fine（最高品质）+ art：处在价值序列顶端的艺术。

normal.en: The phrase translates French beaux-arts, literally 'beautiful arts'.
normal.cn: 这个短语译自法语 beaux-arts，字面是「美的艺术」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: fine art gallery, fine art photography, the fine art market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：美术画廊、艺术摄影、美术市场。

normal.en: The family runs fine, fine arts, fine artist and beaux-arts.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 fine、fine arts、fine artist 与 beaux-arts。

normal.en: The idiom the fine art of... borrows the prestige of the category for ordinary delicacy.
normal.cn: 固定说法 the fine art of... 把类别的声望借给日常的精细手艺。

abstract.en: Picture an object put on a pedestal precisely because it is useless.
abstract.cn: 想象一件正因为它没用而被放上台座的物品。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn between a bowl and a painting, and both sides arguing.
abstract.cn: 想象一条画在碗与画之间的线，两边都在争论。

abstract.en: Picture a certificate that says the object may be looked at, not used.
abstract.cn: 想象一张证书，写明这件东西可供观看，不可使用。

examples.en: Fine art training begins with drawing, whatever medium follows.
examples.cn: 美术训练从素描开始，之后才分媒介。

examples.en: The gallery's fine art collection is shown beside its design archive.
examples.cn: 画廊的美术收藏与设计档案并置展出。

examples.en: He admired the fine art with which she ended the meeting.
examples.cn: 他佩服她结束会议时那份精细的分寸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fine（精细的）+ art（艺术）」——做得精细的艺术 → 美术

root: fine 经古法语 fin「精炼的、最高品质的」上溯拉丁 finis「终点、边界」；art 来自拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺」。fine art 约 1760 年译自法语 beaux-arts。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the category to its disciplines, one work, the border with craft, the market, photography's argument, academic training and finally the idiom of delicate skill.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从类别转到各门学科、单件作品、与工艺的界线、市场、摄影之争、学院训练，最后落到精细技艺的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object that is not for use is placed on a pedestal so that it can be looked at.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件不供使用的物品被放上台座，只为让人观看。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY AND ITS DISCIPLINES: one name, then a list of media.
branches.cn: 类别及其学科：一个名称，然后是一串媒介。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the category applied to a single piece.
branches.cn: 物件：类别被用于单件作品。

branches.en: THE BORDER: the category exists by separating itself from craft.
branches.cn: 边界：类别通过与工艺分离而存在。

branches.en: MARKET AND ARGUMENT: authenticated originals, and the medium that fought for entry.
branches.cn: 市场与争论：经认证的原作，以及为进入而抗争的媒介。

branches.en: TRAINING AND PHRASE: the academy's curriculum, then the idiom of delicate skill.
branches.cn: 训练与说法：学院的课程，然后是精细技艺的固定表达。

intro.en: Fine art is a two-word phrase, not a derivational family; its first element is a French adjective of quality and its second a Latin noun of skill.
intro.cn: fine art 是两词短语，而非派生词族；第一个成分是表示品质的法语形容词，第二个是表示技艺的拉丁名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis and ars are the deep sources, but the phrase itself was formed in French and English, not in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 finis 与 ars 是深层来源，但短语本身是在法语与英语中形成的，不在拉丁语中。

items.structure: Old French fin, from Latin finis (end, limit)

items.exampleCN: 这里的 fine 指精炼，而非纤细。

items.example: Art supplies the second element.
items.exampleCN: art 提供第二个成分。

items.meaning: art of beauty rather than use
items.meaningCN: 以美而非实用为目的的艺术
items.example: Fine art was separated from craft.
items.exampleCN: 美术与工艺被分开。

items.example: The faculty lists the fine arts separately.
items.exampleCN: 学院把各门美术分列。

items.example: The fine artist works in bronze.
items.exampleCN: 这位美术家做青铜。

items.example: The suffix names the person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名人。

items.example: The school kept its French name.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校保留了法语名称。

items.example: The frame is an artistic choice.
items.exampleCN: 画框是一种艺术选择。

definition_zh: 绘画；油画；画作；（上漆的）涂装
definition_en: the art or activity of making pictures with paint, a picture made in this way, or the act of coating a surface with paint
core_image: 一支笔蘸着湿颜料在布上走过，留下一条再也改不回原样的痕迹
scene: 展厅里，修复师在斜射灯下检查一幅画的裂纹，判断清漆是否该去掉。The conservator examined the painting under raking light.
sceneCN: 这里 painting 指「一幅画作」（第 1 个义项：用颜料绘成的图画）；句意为修复师在斜射光下检查这幅画，判断裂纹与清漆状况。

pos.zh: 绘画（艺术或活动）；画作；涂装

derivatives.zh: paint + -er（人）→ 画家／油漆工；从「动作」转到「施事者」
paint + -ed（过去分词）→ 涂过漆的；从「动作」转到「状态」
paint + work（成品）→ 漆面；从「涂料」转到「涂装结果」
painter + -ly（形容词）→ 有绘画笔触感的；从「人」转到「画面质感」

senses.title: A painted picture
senses.definition: a picture made with paint, especially on canvas or panel
senses.definitionCN: 用颜料绘成的图画，尤指画在布面或木板上
senses.example: The conservator examined the painting under raking light.
senses.exampleCN: 修复师在斜射光下检查这幅画。
senses.why: The noun of result names the finished object: what the verb paint produces, treated as a thing that can hang on a wall.
senses.whyCN: 结果名词命名完成的物件：动词 paint 所产出之物，被当作可以挂上墙的东西。

senses.title: The art form
senses.definition: the art of making pictures with paint, considered as a discipline
senses.definitionCN: 用颜料作画的艺术，作为一门学科来看
senses.example: Painting is older than photography by many centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 绘画比摄影早了许多个世纪。
senses.why: The same result-noun can name the whole practice, because a body of works defines a discipline.
senses.whyCN: 同一个结果名词也能命名整个实践，因为一批作品就界定了一门学科。

senses.title: The act of painting
senses.definition: the activity or process of making a picture with paint
senses.definitionCN: 用颜料制作图画的行动或过程
senses.example: Painting takes patience before it takes skill.
senses.exampleCN: 作画先要耐心，然后才谈技巧。
senses.why: The verbal noun also names the ongoing action, not only its outcome; English -ing forms routinely hold both readings.
senses.whyCN: 动名词也命名进行中的动作，而不只是结果；英语 -ing 形式通常同时容纳两种读法。

senses.title: A school or period style
senses.definition: the characteristic style of a school, region or period
senses.definitionCN: 某个画派、地区或时期的典型风格
senses.example: Dutch painting of the golden age is full of reflected light.
senses.exampleCN: 黄金时代的荷兰绘画充满反射光。
senses.why: A mass of works made in one place and time shows shared habits, so the noun can name a style rather than one picture.
senses.whyCN: 一地一时的大量作品显出共同习惯，因此这个名词能命名一种风格，而非一幅画。

senses.title: A subject category
senses.definition: a genre defined by subject, as in portrait painting or landscape painting
senses.definitionCN: 按题材界定的画类，如肖像画或风景画
senses.example: Portrait painting paid better than landscape in his day.
senses.exampleCN: 在他那个年代，肖像画比风景画更赚钱。
senses.why: Genres are compounds built on the noun: the subject in front narrows the art form to one marketable kind.
senses.whyCN: 画类是以这个名词构成的复合词：前面的题材把艺术门类收窄为一种可售卖的类别。

senses.title: Paintwork on a surface
senses.definition: the coating of paint on a building or object
senses.definitionCN: 建筑或物件表面的涂料层
senses.example: The painting of the bridge takes six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的涂装要六周。
senses.why: Because the verb also means 'coat a surface', the noun can name the layer applied, not a picture at all.
senses.whyCN: 因为动词也指「涂覆表面」，名词便能命名所涂的层，与图画无关。

senses.title: The coating trade
senses.definition: the trade or industry of applying paint to surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 把涂料施于表面的行业
senses.example: Industrial painting moved to the new shed.
senses.exampleCN: 工业涂装搬到了新厂房。
senses.why: An activity repeated for hire becomes an industry, so the -ing noun names the trade as well as the act.
senses.whyCN: 为报酬反复进行的活动会变成行业，因此 -ing 名词既命名动作，也命名行业。

senses.title: A medium or technique
senses.definition: a particular medium or technique, as in oil painting or watercolour painting
senses.definitionCN: 某种特定媒介或技法，如油画或水彩画
senses.example: She works in oil painting but teaches drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 她画油画，但教的是素描。
senses.why: The medium in front of the noun turns the art form into a technique: what the paint is made of changes how the picture is made.
senses.whyCN: 名词前的媒介把艺术门类变成一种技法：颜料由什么构成，改变了画如何被制作。

intro.en: Painting is the verbal noun of paint, recorded around 1200; paint came through Old French from Latin pingere, whose deeper root is reconstructed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: painting 是 paint 的动名词，约 1200 年有记录；paint 经古法语来自拉丁 pingere，其更早词根属重构。年代均为约数。

items.en: Reconstructed root *peig- meant 'to cut, mark by incision'; the step from 'decorate with cut marks' to 'decorate with colour' is presumed rather than attested.
items.cn: 重构词根 *peig- 意为「切、刻痕」；从「以刻痕装饰」到「以色彩装饰」的演变是推测，而非有直接书证。

items.en: Pingere meant 'to paint, represent in a picture, stain; embroider, tattoo'.
items.cn: pingere 意为「绘画、在图中表现、染色；刺绣、纹身」。

items.en: Old French peindre 'to paint' supplied the past participle peint, from which English paint derives.
items.cn: 古法语 peindre「绘画」提供过去分词 peint，英语 paint 由此而来。

items.en: English paint is recorded from the mid-thirteenth century, first for representing someone or something in paint.
items.cn: 英语 paint 自 13 世纪中叶有记录，最初指用颜料表现某人或某物。

items.en: Painting is recorded around 1200 for 'that which is painted, a picture'; by the late fourteenth century it also meant the art of depicting with paint.
items.cn: painting 约 1200 年有记录，指「被画成之物、图画」；到 14 世纪后期也指用颜料描绘的艺术。

items.en: From the general verb sense 'cover a surface with colour', the noun acquired the paintwork and trade senses.
items.cn: 从动词的一般义「用颜色覆盖表面」，名词获得了涂层与行业义。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same paint- stock that differ in word class or result; group two holds words for pictures and surfaces made in other ways.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 paint- 词干、但词类或结果不同的词；第二组是用其他方式制作的图画与表面。

entries.definition: The person who paints; painting is the activity or its product.
entries.definitionCN: 作画或涂漆的人；painting 是活动或其产物。

entries.definition: To coat or depict, or the substance used; painting adds the result or activity suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 涂覆或描绘，或所用材料；painting 加上结果或活动后缀。

entries.definition: Describes a surface that has received paint; it is a participle, not a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已上漆的表面；是分词，而非名词。

entries.definition: Describes visible brushwork and a picture-like quality; it is a style judgement, not a category.
entries.definitionCN: 描述可见笔触与画面感；是风格判断，不是类别。

entries.definition: A picture made with lines, usually dry media; painting works with liquid colour and surface.
entries.definitionCN: 用线条、通常以干性媒材作的画；painting 使用液体颜料与表面。

entries.definition: Any visual representation, including photographs and prints; painting specifies the medium.
entries.definitionCN: 任何视觉再现，包括照片与版画；painting 限定媒介。

entries.definition: The woven surface for a painting, or a painting by metonymy; it names the support rather than the art.
entries.definitionCN: 绘画所用的织布表面，或以转喻指一幅画；命名的是支撑物而非艺术。

entries.definition: A layer of material covering a surface; it is the technical cousin of the paintwork sense.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖表面的材料层；是 painting 涂装义的技术近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: paint + -ing: the activity or the thing made.
normal.cn: paint + -ing：活动，或做出来的东西。

normal.en: Latin pingere is the source, and the same stem gives picture and pigment.
normal.cn: 来源是拉丁 pingere，同一词干还给出 picture 与 pigment。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: oil painting, portrait painting, the painting of the bridge.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：油画、肖像画、桥梁涂装。

normal.en: The family runs paint, painter, painting, painted, paintwork and painterly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 paint、painter、painting、painted、paintwork 与 painterly。

normal.en: A museum label says 'oil on canvas' but calls the object a painting.
normal.cn: 博物馆标签写「布面油画」，却把对象称作 painting。

abstract.en: Picture a wet stroke that cannot be undone without leaving a trace.
abstract.cn: 想象一道湿笔触，想撤掉总会留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture a flat surface becoming a window that is also an object.
abstract.cn: 想象一块平面变成既是窗又是物的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a wall and a canvas answering to the same action.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙与一块画布回应同一个动作。

examples.en: The painting was relined before the exhibition.
examples.cn: 这幅画在展览前做了托裱。

examples.en: Painting was taught alongside anatomy in the old academy.
examples.cn: 在旧式学院里，绘画与解剖学一起教授。

examples.en: The painting of the hall took longer than the carpentry.
examples.cn: 大厅的涂装比木工花的时间更长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「paint（涂颜料）+ -ing」——涂出来的东西 → 画

root: 拉丁 pingere「绘画、染色」经古法语 peindre、过去分词 peint 进入英语 paint（13 世纪中叶）；painting 约 1200 年出现，兼指画作、绘画艺术与涂装。更早词根拟为 *peig-「刻痕」，属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the finished picture to the art form, the act, a school, a genre, a painted surface, the coating trade and a specific medium.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从完成的画作转到艺术门类、行为、画派、画类、涂层、涂装行业与具体媒介。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brush loaded with wet pigment crosses the cloth and leaves a mark that cannot return to nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支蘸满湿颜料的笔走过布面，留下一条无法回到空白的痕迹。

branches.en: THE PICTURE: the result, hanging on a wall.
branches.cn: 画作：结果，挂在墙上。

branches.en: ART AND MEDIUM: the whole discipline, then one technique inside it.
branches.cn: 艺术与媒介：整门学科，然后是其中一种技法。

branches.en: THE ACT: the doing, which the same suffix also names.
branches.cn: 行为：正在做的过程，同一后缀也能命名它。

branches.en: SCHOOL AND GENRE: shared habits across works, then a subject category.
branches.cn: 画派与画类：作品间的共同习惯，然后是题材类别。

branches.en: THE SURFACE TRADE: coating an object, then the industry that does it for hire.
branches.cn: 表面行业：给物件上涂层，然后是为报酬做这件事的行业。

intro.en: Painting is a verb stem plus the noun suffix -ing, and the stem builds a family of people, results and styles.
intro.cn: painting 是动词词干加名词后缀 -ing，同一词干还构成指人、结果与风格的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin pingere is the ancestor; it also yields picture, pigment and depict, all through the idea of marking a surface.
latinIntro.cn: 祖先是拉丁 pingere；它还给出 picture、pigment 与 depict，都经由「在表面留下痕迹」这一观念。

items.structure: Old French peindre, from Latin pingere
items.meaning: to colour a surface; to depict
items.example: They painted the door blue.
items.exampleCN: 他们把门漆成蓝色。

items.example: Building and painting use the same ending.
items.exampleCN: building 与 painting 用同一个词尾。

items.meaning: a picture; the art or act
items.example: The painting hangs in the north room.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画挂在北厅。

items.example: The painter primed the wall.
items.exampleCN: 油漆工给墙上了底漆。

items.example: The painted shutters were new.
items.exampleCN: 上过漆的百叶窗是新的。

items.meaning: the painted surface of an object
items.example: The paintwork was chipped at the edge.
items.exampleCN: 边缘的漆面有剥落。

items.example: The photograph has a painterly softness.
items.exampleCN: 这张照片有一种绘画般的柔和。

items.meaning: to portray in an image or words
items.example: The seal depicts a lion.
items.exampleCN: 这枚印章描绘一头狮子。

items.example: The pigment faded in the light.
items.exampleCN: 颜料在光下褪色。

items.example: The picture shows the harbour.
items.exampleCN: 这幅图画显示港口。

definition_en: an artist who paints pictures, or a worker who paints surfaces
core_image: 同一只手，一边在画布上安排颜色，一边在墙上把颜色铺平
scene: 装修现场，工人把梯子挪到墙边，准备刷第二遍。The painter moved the ladder and began the second coat.
sceneCN: 这里 painter 指「以粉刷、涂漆为业的工人」（第 2 个义项：给建筑表面涂漆的油漆工）；句意为油漆工挪好梯子，开始刷第二遍。

derivatives.zh: paint + -ing（动作或结果）→ 绘画；从「人」转到「活动与产物」
painter + -ly（形容词）→ 有笔触感的；从「人」转到「画面风格」
paint + work（成品）→ 漆面；从「动作」转到「表面结果」
paint + -ed（分词）→ 上过漆的；从「动作」转到「状态」

senses.title: An artist who paints pictures
senses.definition: a person who makes pictures with paint as an artist
senses.definitionCN: 以绘画为艺术创作的人
senses.example: The painter worked standing up, with the canvas on an easel.
senses.exampleCN: 这位画家站着作画，画布放在画架上。
senses.why: The agent suffix -er turns paint into 'one who paints'; in the art world that person is the maker of pictures.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀 -er 把 paint 变成「涂绘的人」；在艺术界，这个人就是图画的制作者。

senses.title: A worker who paints surfaces
senses.definition: a tradesperson who applies paint to buildings and other surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 给建筑及其他表面涂漆的行业工人
senses.example: The painter moved the ladder and began the second coat.
senses.exampleCN: 油漆工挪好梯子，开始刷第二遍。
senses.why: The verb's everyday sense is 'coat a surface', so the same agent noun also names the trade that does it for pay.
senses.whyCN: 动词的日常义是「涂覆表面」，因此同一个施事名词也命名以此为报酬的行业。

senses.title: An artist known for a subject
senses.titleCN: 以某类题材著称的画家
senses.definition: an artist identified with a particular subject or genre
senses.definitionCN: 与某一题材或画类紧密相连的艺术家
senses.example: He was a painter of harbours before he was a painter of battles.
senses.exampleCN: 他先是画港口的画家，后来才画战役。
senses.why: The of-phrase narrows the artist's identity to what he habitually depicts, a common way of naming artistic specialism.
senses.whyCN: of 短语把艺术家的身份收窄到他惯常描绘之物，这是命名艺术专长的常见方式。

senses.title: An artist known for a medium
senses.titleCN: 以某种媒介著称的画家
senses.definition: an artist identified with a particular medium, as in oil painter
senses.definitionCN: 与某种媒介相连的艺术家，如油画家
senses.example: As an oil painter she distrusted quick sketches.
senses.exampleCN: 作为油画家，她不信任快速素描。
senses.why: Compounds put the medium before the agent, so the painter is defined by the material whose craft he has mastered.
senses.whyCN: 复合词把媒介放在施事者前，因此画家由他所精通的材料来界定。

senses.title: A painter in art history
senses.definition: a painter as a historical figure studied in art history
senses.definitionCN: 作为艺术史研究对象的历史人物
senses.example: The catalogue lists every painter represented in the collection.
senses.exampleCN: 图录列出了收藏中出现的每一位画家。
senses.why: The discipline turns individual makers into catalogue entries and attributions, so painter becomes a historical category.
senses.whyCN: 学科把个体创作者变成图录条目与归属判断，因此 painter 成为历史类别。

senses.title: An amateur or hobby painter
senses.definition: a person who paints for pleasure rather than professionally
senses.definitionCN: 为乐趣而非职业作画的人
senses.example: My uncle is a painter on Sundays and a clerk all week.
senses.exampleCN: 我叔叔周日是画家，其余时间是小职员。
senses.why: An agent noun does not require payment, so anyone who performs the action can be called a painter, including a hobbyist.
senses.whyCN: 施事名词不要求报酬，因此任何执行该动作的人都能被称为 painter，包括业余爱好者。

senses.title: A sign or lettering painter
senses.definition: a craftsman who paints signs, lettering or decorative surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 绘制招牌、字体或装饰表面的工匠
senses.example: The sign painter lettered the shop window by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 招牌画工用手工给橱窗写字。
senses.why: Compound specialisms preserve older workshop senses: the painter is the skilled hand in a named trade, not necessarily a fine artist.
senses.whyCN: 复合专名保留较早的工坊义：painter 是某个具名行当里的熟练手，不一定是纯艺术家。

senses.title: A workshop painter
senses.definition: a painter employed in a master's workshop to execute parts of works
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于名家工坊、执行作品局部的画师
senses.example: Many panels were finished by a workshop painter rather than the master.
senses.exampleCN: 许多木板画是由工坊画师而非名家本人完成的。
senses.why: Before the modern studio, paintings were made by teams; the word names each hand in the division of labour.
senses.whyCN: 在现代工作室出现之前，绘画由团队完成；这个词命名分工中的每一只手。

intro.en: Painter comes from Old French peintor, from Latin pictor, an agent noun from pingere 'to paint'; a separate homograph for a boat rope has a different origin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: painter 来自古法语 peintor，上溯拉丁 pictor，即 pingere「绘画」的施事名词；另有一个指船缆的同形词，来源不同。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pingere meant 'to paint, depict, stain'; its deeper root is reconstructed as *peig- 'to cut, mark'.
items.cn: pingere 意为「绘画、描绘、染色」；其更早词根拟为 *peig-「切、刻痕」。

items.en: Pictor was the agent noun 'painter', formed from the stem of pingere; it named both the artist and the craftsman.
items.cn: pictor 是施事名词「画家」，由 pingere 的词干构成；既指艺术家，也指工匠。

items.en: Old French peintor carried the word into English; the same French form also named a rope on a boat, a confusing coincidence of spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 peintor 把这个词带入英语；同一法语形式还指船上的一条缆绳，这是令人困惑的拼写巧合。

items.en: English painter is recorded in the early fourteenth century as 'artist who paints pictures'.
items.cn: 英语 painter 于 14 世纪初有记录，指「作画的艺术家」。

items.en: By about 1400 the word also meant 'workman who colours surfaces with paint'.
items.cn: 到约 1400 年，这个词也指「用颜料给表面着色的工人」。

items.en: The rope painter of the mid-fourteenth century probably comes from a different Old French word and ultimately from Latin pendere 'to hang'; that path is uncertain, and the two words are unrelated despite identical spelling.
items.cn: 14 世纪中叶指缆绳的 painter 可能来自另一个古法语词，最终上溯拉丁 pendere「悬挂」；这条路径不确定，两个词尽管拼写相同却并不同源。

note.en: Group one holds the same-stem words and the unrelated rope homograph; group two holds occupations and art roles that overlap but stress a different material or setting.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干词以及无关的缆绳同形词；第二组是重叠但强调不同材料或场景的职业与艺术角色。

entries.definition: A rope used to tie a boat; it is a homograph, not a sense of the artist word, and comes probably from Latin pendere 'to hang'.
entries.definitionCN: 系船的缆绳；是同形异源词，不是艺术家一词的义项，可能来自拉丁 pendere「悬挂」。

entries.definition: A picture or the activity of painting; painter is the person who performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 画作或绘画活动；painter 是执行它的人。

entries.definition: To coat or depict, or the coloured substance; painter is the agent.
entries.definitionCN: 涂覆或描绘，或彩色材料；painter 是施事者。

entries.definition: Having visible brushwork or a soft, painted quality; it describes a surface, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 有可见笔触或柔和绘画感的；描述表面，而非人。

entries.definition: A maker of art in any medium; painter is the narrower word for one who works in paint.
entries.definitionCN: 任何媒介的艺术创作者；painter 是专指用颜料者的较窄词。

entries.definition: A worker who paints and papers interiors; painter stresses the paintwork, decorator the whole finish.
entries.definitionCN: 给室内刷漆贴墙纸的工人；painter 强调涂漆，decorator 强调整体饰面。

entries.definition: A painter who works on walls; painter is neutral about scale or support.
entries.definitionCN: 在墙上作画的画家；painter 对尺幅与支撑物不加限定。

entries.definition: A painter or photographer specialising in portraits; painter names no subject.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻肖像的画家或摄影师；painter 不限定题材。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: paint + -er 'one who': the person who paints, whether canvas or wall.
normal.cn: paint + -er「从事者」：涂绘的人，无论画布还是墙面。

normal.en: Latin pictor is the ancestor, and picture and pigment share the stem.
normal.cn: 祖先是拉丁 pictor，picture 与 pigment 共享同一词干。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: portrait painter, house painter, sign painter.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：肖像画家、房屋油漆工、招牌画工。

normal.en: The family runs paint, painter, painting, painted and painterly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 paint、painter、painting、painted 与 painterly。

normal.en: The rope painter is a different word: same spelling, different origin, no family relation.
normal.cn: 指缆绳的 painter 是另一个词：拼写相同、来源不同、没有亲缘关系。

abstract.en: Picture one hand that can both compose a face and flatten a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象同一只手既能安排一张脸，也能把一面墙铺平。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder standing where an easel might also stand.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子立在本可放画架的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a name that two unrelated things have learned to share.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被两件无关之物共用的名字。

examples.en: The painter left the canvas unfinished when the light changed.
examples.cn: 光线一变，画家就停下未完成的画。

examples.en: A painter and decorator was repainting the stairwell.
examples.cn: 一位油漆装饰工正在重刷楼梯间。

examples.en: The workshop painter filled in the background while the master worked on the face.
examples.cn: 名家画脸时，工坊画师补画背景。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「paint（涂颜料）+ -er（人）」——涂颜料的人 → 画家／油漆工

root: 拉丁 pingere「绘画、染色」的施事名词 pictor，经古法语 peintor 进入英语，14 世纪初指画家，约 1400 年兼指油漆工。指船缆的 painter 为同形异源词，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses distinguish the fine artist from the trade worker, then split by subject, medium, historical role, amateur status, sign work and workshop division of labour.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把纯艺术家与行业工人分开，再按题材、媒介、历史角色、业余身份、招牌工作与工坊分工细分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand arranges colour on a canvas and flattens colour on a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一只手在画布上安排颜色，也在墙上把颜色铺平。

branches.en: THE PICTURE MAKER: the artist whose product is an image.
branches.cn: 作画者：产物是一幅图像的艺术家。

branches.en: THE SURFACE COATER: the same agent noun in the building trade.
branches.cn: 表面涂覆者：同一施事名词在建筑行业中的用法。

branches.en: SUBJECT: identity narrowed to what is depicted.
branches.cn: 题材：身份被收窄到所描绘之物。

branches.en: MEDIUM AND HISTORY: the material mastered, then the figure in the catalogue.
branches.cn: 媒介与历史：所精通的材料，然后是图录中的人物。

branches.en: ROLES AROUND THE CRAFT: amateur, sign worker and workshop hand.
branches.cn: 手艺周边的角色：业余者、招牌工与工坊画师。

intro.en: Painter is a verb stem plus the agent suffix -er; the stem's Latin ancestor builds a whole family of images, materials and actions.
intro.cn: painter 是动词词干加施事后缀 -er；其词干的拉丁祖先构成一整族图像、材料与动作词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pictor is the direct model; pingere also yields picture, pigment, depict and pictorial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pictor 是直接模板；pingere 还给出 picture、pigment、depict 与 pictorial。

items.structure: Old French peindre, from Latin pingere
