items.exampleCN: 她在上午作画。

items.example: Painter follows the pattern of builder.
items.exampleCN: painter 沿用了 builder 的模式。

items.example: The painter signed the lower corner.
items.exampleCN: 画家在下角签了名。

items.example: Painting was her only subject.
items.exampleCN: 绘画是她唯一的科目。

items.example: The sky is handled in a painterly way.
items.exampleCN: 天空以绘画式手法处理。

items.example: The painted cloth hung behind the altar.
items.exampleCN: 画过的布挂在祭坛后。

items.example: The paintwork needs repair.
items.exampleCN: 漆面需要修补。

items.example: The frieze depicts a procession.
items.exampleCN: 壁带描绘一支游行队伍。

items.example: The pigment is ground by hand.
items.exampleCN: 颜料用手工研磨。

items.example: The picture is older than the frame.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画比画框更古老。

definition_zh: 肖像；画像；人像照片；人物描绘
definition_en: a painting, drawing or photograph of a person, especially of the face, or a description that captures someone's character
core_image: 一张脸被固定在一个姿势里，眼神却继续朝外看
scene: 摄影棚里，摄影师请她略微转头，让光落在颧骨上。The photographer asked her to turn slightly so the portrait caught the light.
sceneCN: 这里 portrait 指「人像照片」（第 2 个义项：以相机拍摄的人物肖像）；句意为摄影师请她略微转头，好让这张人像接住光。

pos.zh: 肖像；画像；人像照片；文字描绘；（纸张的）竖幅

derivatives.zh: portray + -al（名词后缀）→ 描绘出的形象；从「再现动作」转到「产出的形象」
portrait + -ist（从业者）→ 肖像画家；从「作品」转到「作者」
portrait + -ure（行为或结果）→ 肖像画艺术；从「单件」转到「整个实践」
self- + portrait → 自画像；从「他人肖像」转到「自我再现」

senses.title: A painted or drawn image of a person
senses.definition: a painting or drawing representing a person, especially the face
senses.definitionCN: 表现一个人、尤以面部为主的绘画或素描
senses.example: The portrait shows a merchant holding a letter.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅肖像画着一位手持信件的商人。
senses.why: Portrait began as a noun from the verb 'to draw forth'; the drawn likeness of a person is the core that all other senses extend.
senses.whyCN: portrait 最初是动词「拉出、描绘」的名词化；一个人的被描绘形象是其余义项所扩展的核心。

senses.title: A photographic likeness
senses.definition: a photograph of a person, usually posed and framed
senses.definitionCN: 通常经过摆拍与取景的人物照片
senses.example: The photographer asked her to turn slightly so the portrait caught the light.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师请她略微转头，好让这张人像接住光。
senses.why: When photography arrived, the old word for a drawn likeness transferred to the camera: the medium changed, the social function did not.
senses.whyCN: 摄影出现后，旧有的「绘制形象」一词转到相机上：媒介变了，社会功能没变。

senses.title: A description in words
senses.definition: a literary description that captures a person's appearance and character
senses.definitionCN: 在文学中捕捉一个人外貌与性格的描写
senses.example: The novel opens with a portrait of the aunt at her piano.
senses.exampleCN: 小说开篇是姑妈坐在钢琴前的一幅文字肖像。
senses.why: The metaphor 'portrait in words' treats language as a surface that can hold a likeness, an extension recorded in the eighteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 「文字中的肖像」这一隐喻把语言当作能承载形象的表面，这一扩展在 18 世纪有记录。

senses.title: A filmic depiction of a place or group
senses.titleCN: 影视对地点或群体的描绘
senses.definition: a film or television work that depicts a place, community or period in depth
senses.definitionCN: 深入描绘一个地点、群体或时期的电影或电视作品
senses.example: The documentary is a portrait of a fishing town in decline.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片是一个衰落渔港的肖像。
senses.why: The sense widens from a person to any subject treated as a character: a place can be given a face by a film.
senses.whyCN: 词义从人扩展到任何被当作角色处理的对象：一部影片可以给一个地方一张脸。

senses.title: The genre in art history
senses.titleCN: 艺术史中的肖像画门类
senses.definition: the genre of portraiture as classified in art history
senses.definitionCN: 艺术史分类中的肖像画门类
senses.example: Portrait was ranked below history painting in the academy.
senses.exampleCN: 在学院体系里，肖像画的等级低于历史画。
senses.why: A kind of work becomes a genre, so the noun can name the category rather than one object.
senses.whyCN: 一类作品会变成一个门类，因此这个名词能命名类别，而非单件作品。

senses.title: A likeness in any medium
senses.titleCN: 任何媒介中的相似形象
senses.definition: a representation of a person's appearance in any medium
senses.definitionCN: 在任何媒介中对一个人外貌的再现
senses.example: The coin bears a portrait in low relief.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚钱币上有浅浮雕肖像。
senses.why: Once the word means 'likeness', the material is free: paint, stone, metal and pixels can all carry a portrait.
senses.whyCN: 一旦词义是「相似形象」，材料就不受限制：颜料、石头、金属与像素都能承载肖像。

senses.title: Vertical page or screen format
senses.definition: the upright orientation of a page, photograph or screen
senses.definitionCN: 页面、照片或屏幕的竖直方向
senses.example: Switch the page to portrait before printing.
senses.exampleCN: 打印前把页面改成竖幅。
senses.why: A portrait painting is typically taller than it is wide, so the format inherited the name of its usual subject.
senses.whyCN: 肖像画通常高大于宽，因此这种版式继承了其常见题材的名称。

senses.title: A sculpted head or bust
senses.definition: a sculpted head or bust representing a person
senses.definitionCN: 表现一个人的雕塑头部或胸像
senses.example: A marble portrait of the founder stands in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 一尊创始人的大理石胸像立在大厅里。
senses.why: Sculpture adopts the word because the aim is still a recognisable person, even when the medium is stone rather than paint.
senses.whyCN: 雕塑采用这个词，因为目标仍是可辨认的个人，即使媒介是石头而非颜料。

intro.en: Portrait came into English in the sixteenth century from French, ultimately from Latin protrahere 'to draw forth'; it is a doublet of portray. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: portrait 于 16 世纪从法语进入英语，最终来自拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」；它与 portray 是同源双重词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Protrahere meant 'to draw forth, drag out, reveal'; it joined pro- 'forth' to trahere 'to draw, drag'.
items.cn: protrahere 意为「拉出、拖出、显露」，由 pro-「向前」与 trahere「拉、拖」组合。

items.en: Old French portraire meant 'to draw, paint, portray', literally 'to trace forth'; medieval Latin also used protrahere for painting.
items.cn: 古法语 portraire 意为「画、描绘」，字面是「向前描出」；中世纪拉丁也用 protrahere 指绘画。

items.en: Old French portret, the past participle of portraire used as a noun, named a drawn or painted figure.
items.cn: 古法语 portret 是 portraire 的过去分词名词化，指被绘制的人物形象。

items.en: English portrait is recorded in the 1560s as 'a figure drawn or painted', a back-formation from portraiture or a direct borrowing from French.
items.cn: 英语 portrait 于 16 世纪 60 年代有记录，指「被绘制的人物形象」，或由 portraiture 逆构，或直接借自法语。

items.en: The sense narrowed to the head and face represented from life, which became the central everyday meaning.
items.cn: 词义收窄到写生表现的头部与面部，这成为日常核心义。

items.en: Photography, film and printing extended the word to camera likenesses, depictions of places and vertical page formats.
items.cn: 摄影、电影与印刷把这个词扩展到相机拍摄的肖像、地点描绘与竖幅版式。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words that are constantly confused with portrait; group two holds nouns for likenesses that differ in medium or scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、常与 portrait 混淆的词；第二组是不同媒介或范围的人物再现名词。

entries.definition: The art of making portraits, or portraits collectively; portrait is one work.
entries.definitionCN: 制作肖像的艺术，或肖像总称；portrait 是一件作品。

entries.definition: To depict in a picture or words; portrait is the resulting noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在图画或文字中描绘；portrait 是结果名词。

entries.definition: A painter or photographer who specialises in portraits; the word names the person, not the work.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻肖像的画家或摄影师；这个名词指人，而非作品。

entries.definition: A portrait in which the artist depicts himself or herself; it is a compound of portrait with self.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术家描绘自己的肖像；是 portrait 与 self 的复合词。

entries.definition: The quality of looking like someone, or an image that resembles them; it need not be a formal portrait.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像某人的性质，或相似的形象；不一定是正式肖像。

entries.definition: A general visual representation; portrait specifies that the subject is a person.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指视觉再现；portrait 限定对象是人。

entries.definition: A sculpture of a person's head and shoulders; portrait includes painted, photographed and full-figure works.
entries.definitionCN: 人物头肩部的雕塑；portrait 还包括绘画、摄影与全身作品。

entries.definition: A side view of a face, or a short biographical sketch; a portrait may be frontal or in profile.
entries.definitionCN: 脸的侧面，或简短生平；肖像可以是正面或侧面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin protrahere 'draw forth' gives both portrait and portray.
normal.cn: 拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」同时给出 portrait 与 portray。

normal.en: The noun is a past participle turned into a thing: 'the drawn-out likeness'.
normal.cn: 这个名词是过去分词变成的物件：「被拉出的形象」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: portrait painter, family portrait, portrait mode.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：肖像画家、全家福、竖屏模式。

normal.en: The family runs portrait, portraiture, portraitist, portray and self-portrait.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 portrait、portraiture、portraitist、portray 与 self-portrait。

normal.en: A page taller than wide is in portrait format because portraits usually are.
normal.cn: 高大于宽的页面叫竖幅，因为肖像通常如此。

abstract.en: Picture a face held still while its look continues to move.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被固定住的脸，目光却仍在移动。

abstract.en: Picture a surface that can be paper, canvas, stone or a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一种可以是纸、画布、石头或屏幕的表面。

abstract.en: Picture a likeness that survives the person it shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个比被描绘者活得更久的形象。

examples.en: The portrait was cleaned and the varnish removed.
examples.cn: 这幅肖像经过清洗，清漆被去掉。

examples.en: He wrote a portrait of his father that avoided sentiment.
examples.cn: 他写下一篇避免感伤的父亲肖像。

examples.en: The stamp carries a portrait engraved from a photograph.
examples.cn: 这枚邮票上有一幅依据照片雕刻的肖像。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「por（向前）+ trait（拉）」——把人的样子拉出来 → 肖像

root: 拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」（pro- 向前 + trahere 拉）经古法语 portraire、过去分词 portret，16 世纪 60 年代进入英语为 portrait；与 portray 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the drawn face to the photograph, the verbal description, the filmic place, the genre, any likeness, the vertical format and the sculpted bust.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从绘制的脸出发，转到照片、文字描写、影视地点、艺术门类、任何媒介的相似形象、竖幅版式与雕塑胸像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face is fixed in a pose while its gaze keeps looking outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张脸被固定在一个姿势里，目光却继续朝外看。

branches.en: THE LIKENESS IN MATTER: painted or sculpted, both aim at a recognisable person.
branches.cn: 材料中的形象：绘画或雕塑，目标都是可辨认的个人。

branches.en: THE CAMERA: the drawn likeness becomes a photographic one.
branches.cn: 相机：被绘制的形象变成照片。

branches.en: IN WORDS AND ON FILM: a person described, then a place given a face.
branches.cn: 文字与影片：先描写一个人，再给一个地方一张脸。

branches.en: CATEGORY AND MEDIUM: the genre, then any material that can carry it.
branches.cn: 类别与媒介：先是门类，再是任何能承载它的材料。

branches.en: FORMAT: the upright page inherits the shape of its usual subject.
branches.cn: 版式：竖幅页面继承了其常见题材的形状。

intro.en: Portrait is a Latin participle form borrowed through French; its family includes the verb of depicting and the name of the practice.
intro.cn: portrait 是经法语借入的拉丁分词形式；其词族包括描绘动词与指称这门实践的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin protrahere and trahere supply the root; the -trait ending is the French past-participle shape, not a living English suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 protrahere 与 trahere 提供词根；-trait 词尾是法语过去分词形态，不是能产的英语后缀。

items.example: The prefix contributes the sense of drawing out.
items.exampleCN: 前缀贡献「拉出」之义。

items.example: Trahere also gives tractor and trace.
items.exampleCN: trahere 还给出 tractor 与 trace。

items.example: The verb passed into English as portray.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词进入英语成为 portray。

items.structure: French portrait, past participle of portraire
items.example: The portrait was hung above the fireplace.
items.exampleCN: 这幅肖像挂在壁炉上方。

items.example: The novel portrays the city in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说描绘冬天的城市。

items.example: Portraiture flourished at the court.
items.exampleCN: 肖像艺术在宫廷兴盛。

items.example: The portraitist worked only in pastel.
items.exampleCN: 这位肖像画家只用色粉。

items.example: The self-portrait shows the artist at work.
items.exampleCN: 这幅自画像表现正在作画的艺术家。

definition_zh: 肖像画艺术；肖像画（总称）；人像摄影
definition_en: the art or practice of making portraits, or portraits considered as a group
core_image: 许多张脸在同一面墙上排开，构成一种看人的传统
scene: 美术馆把四个世纪的肖像排成一条线索，从木板画一直排到照片。The exhibition traces four centuries of portraiture, from panel painting to photography.
sceneCN: 这里 portraiture 指「肖像创作这门艺术及其历史实践」（第 1 个义项：制作肖像的艺术）；句意为展览梳理四个世纪的肖像艺术，从木板画直到摄影。

pos.zh: 肖像画艺术；肖像画总称（通常不可数）

forms.label: 可数用法（少见，指多种实践）

derivatives.zh: portraiture 逆构 → 单幅肖像；从「整体实践」转到「一件作品」
portrait + -ist（人）→ 肖像作者；从「实践」转到「从业者」
self- + portraiture → 自我肖像实践；从「他人」转到「自我」

senses.title: The art of making portraits
senses.definition: the art, skill or practice of making portraits
senses.definitionCN: 制作肖像的艺术、技巧或实践
senses.example: The exhibition traces four centuries of portraiture.
senses.exampleCN: 这场展览梳理四个世纪的肖像艺术。
senses.why: The suffix -ure, from Latin -ura, names an activity and its result; added to portrait, it turns one work into the practice that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ure 来自拉丁 -ura，命名活动及其结果；加在 portrait 上，就把单件作品变成生产它的实践。

senses.title: Portraits considered as a group
senses.definition: portraits collectively, especially in a collection or tradition
senses.definitionCN: 肖像作品的集合，尤指一个收藏或传统中的总体
senses.example: The castle's portraiture fills three galleries.
senses.exampleCN: 城堡的肖像藏品装满三个展厅。
senses.why: An uncountable mass noun treats many works as one body, the way furniture gathers many objects.
senses.whyCN: 不可数集合名词把许多作品当作一个整体，正如 furniture 收拢许多物件。

senses.title: A single portrait, in older use
senses.definition: one portrait, a countable use now largely replaced by portrait
senses.definitionCN: 一幅肖像；这一可数用法现在大多被 portrait 取代
senses.example: The inventory lists a portraiture of the duke.
senses.exampleCN: 清单上列有一幅公爵肖像。
senses.why: Before the back-formed portrait spread, portraiture could still mean one picture; the newer word took over the count.
senses.whyCN: 在逆构的 portrait 普及之前，portraiture 仍可指一幅画；较新的词接管了计数功能。

senses.title: A literary portrayal
senses.definition: a description or portrayal of a person in writing
senses.definitionCN: 文字中对一个人的描写或刻画
senses.example: The chapter is a portraiture of the family in one long evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章以漫长的一夜刻画了这个家庭。
senses.why: The metaphor of painting extends to writing: a text can be called a portraiture when it builds a person detail by detail.
senses.whyCN: 绘画的隐喻扩展到写作：当文本逐笔构建一个人物时，就可以被称为一幅 portraiture。

senses.title: The genre in art history
senses.definition: portrait-making as a recognised genre of art
senses.definitionCN: 作为受认可艺术门类的肖像制作
senses.example: Portraiture was ranked below history painting.
senses.exampleCN: 肖像画在等级上低于历史画。
senses.why: Once a practice is classified, its name becomes a genre label in academies and museums.
senses.whyCN: 一旦实践被分类，其名称就成为学院与博物馆中的门类标签。

senses.title: A style or approach within the genre
senses.titleCN: 肖像门类中的风格或路径
senses.definition: a distinctive manner or approach to making portraits
senses.definitionCN: 制作肖像的独特方式或路径
senses.example: Her portraiture avoids the frontal stare.
senses.exampleCN: 她的肖像手法回避正面直视。
senses.why: A practice can be done in different ways, so the mass noun also names a manner, not only the category.
senses.whyCN: 同一实践可以有不同做法，因此这个集合名词也命名一种手法，而不只是类别。

senses.title: The commissioning business
senses.definition: the social and commercial system of commissioning portraits
senses.definitionCN: 委托制作肖像的社会与商业体系
senses.example: Eighteenth-century portraiture depended on aristocratic commissions.
senses.exampleCN: 18 世纪的肖像业依赖贵族委托。
senses.why: Portraits cost money and mark status, so the practice also names the economy of patrons and sitters.
senses.whyCN: 肖像耗资且标示身份，因此这门实践也命名赞助人与被画者构成的经济。

senses.title: Photographic portrait practice
senses.definition: the practice of making portraits with a camera
senses.definitionCN: 用相机制作肖像的实践
senses.example: Studio portraiture moved from painted backdrops to paper rolls.
senses.exampleCN: 影室人像从手绘背景转到纸卷背景。
senses.why: When the camera took over the likeness, the old practice word went with it and named a new medium's version.
senses.whyCN: 当相机接管肖像制作，旧的实践名词也随之而去，命名新媒介中的版本。

intro.en: Portraiture came into English from Old French in the late fourteenth century, from the same verb that gives portray and portrait. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: portraiture 于 14 世纪后期从古法语进入英语，与 portray、portrait 同出一个动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Protrahere 'to draw forth' joined pro- 'forth' and trahere 'to draw'; medieval Latin used it for painting as well as revealing.
items.cn: protrahere「拉出、描绘」由 pro-「向前」与 trahere「拉」组合；中世纪拉丁也用它指绘画，而不只是显露。

items.en: Old French portraire meant 'to draw, paint, portray'; its noun forms supplied both portrait and portraiture.
items.cn: 古法语 portraire 意为「画、描绘」；其名词形式同时提供 portrait 与 portraiture。

items.en: Old French portraiture (twelfth century) meant 'portrait, image, portrayal, resemblance'.
items.cn: 古法语 portraiture（12 世纪）意为「肖像、形象、描绘、相似」。

items.en: English portraiture is recorded in the late fourteenth century for 'the art of making portraits; a painting or drawing'.
items.cn: 英语 portraiture 于 14 世纪后期有记录，指「制作肖像的艺术；一幅绘画或素描」。

items.en: The countable sense 'a portrait' passed to the back-formed portrait in the sixteenth century, leaving portraiture for the art and the collective.
items.cn: 可数义「一幅肖像」在 16 世纪转给逆构的 portrait，portraiture 则保留给艺术与总称。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century photography extended the practice word to camera portraits without changing its core meaning.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪的摄影把这一实践名词扩展到相机肖像，核心意义未变。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root words that differ in count or word class; group two holds labels for the practice seen from other trades.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、但计数或词类不同的词；第二组是从其他行当看待这门实践的标签。

entries.definition: A single likeness; portraiture is the practice or the whole body.
entries.definitionCN: 单件形象；portraiture 是实践或整体。

entries.definition: A maker of portraits; the ending -ist names the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 肖像制作者；词尾 -ist 命名从业者。

entries.definition: To depict a person or scene; portraiture is the resulting practice noun.
entries.definitionCN: 描绘人物或场景；portraiture 是相应的实践名词。

entries.definition: The practice of making portraits of oneself; the compound adds self to the practice word.
entries.definitionCN: 制作自我肖像的实践；复合词在实践名词前加了 self。

entries.definition: Portrait-making in paint specifically; portraiture also covers photography, sculpture and drawing.
entries.definitionCN: 特指用颜料制作肖像；portraiture 还涵盖摄影、雕塑与素描。

entries.definition: The act of representing anything in image or words; portraiture is limited to persons and their likeness.
entries.definitionCN: 以图像或文字再现任何事物的行为；portraiture 限于人物及其形象。

entries.definition: The quality of resembling someone, or an image that does so; portraiture is the organised practice of producing such images.
entries.definitionCN: 相似的性质，或相似的形象；portraiture 是生产此类图像的成体系实践。

entries.definition: Image-making with light; photographic portraiture is one branch of it.
entries.definitionCN: 用光成像；人像摄影是其中的一支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: portrait + -ure: the activity and its accumulated result.
normal.cn: portrait + -ure：活动及其累积结果。

normal.en: The word came through Old French portraiture from portraire, 'to draw forth'.
normal.cn: 这个词经古法语 portraiture 来自 portraire「向前描出」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the practice: the art of portraiture, British portraiture, commissioned portraiture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出实践：肖像艺术、英国肖像画、委托肖像创作。

normal.en: The family runs portrait, portraits, portraitist, portray and self-portraiture.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 portrait、portraits、portraitist、portray 与 self-portraiture。

normal.en: The -ure ending also appears in literature and furniture, both mass-like nouns of activity or result.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ure 也出现在 literature 与 furniture 中，都是偏集合的活动或结果名词。

abstract.en: Picture many faces lined up until they become one tradition.
abstract.cn: 想象许多张脸排成一行，直到变成一种传统。

abstract.en: Picture a practice that outlives every sitter it depicts.
abstract.cn: 想象一门比它所描绘的每位被画者都活得久的实践。

abstract.en: Picture a verb, a single work and a whole wall sharing one root.
abstract.cn: 想象一个动词、一件作品与一整面墙共享同一个词根。

examples.en: Portraiture was the academy's steadiest source of income.
examples.cn: 肖像画是学院最稳定的收入来源。

examples.en: The book surveys portraiture from panel to screen.
examples.cn: 这本书梳理从木板到屏幕的肖像实践。

examples.en: Her portraiture gives equal weight to hands and faces.
examples.cn: 她的肖像手法给手与脸同等的分量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「portrait（肖像）+ -ure（行为/结果）」——画肖像这件事 → 肖像画艺术

root: 拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」经古法语 portraire 与名词 portraiture（12 世纪），14 世纪后期进入英语，指制作肖像的艺术；16 世纪单数义转给 portrait。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the art itself to the collective body, the older single picture, the literary portrayal, the genre, a style, the commissioning economy and photographic practice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从艺术本身转到作品总称、较早的单幅用法、文学刻画、门类、风格、委托经济与摄影实践。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many faces are lined up on one wall until they form a way of looking at people.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多张脸在同一面墙上排开，直到构成一种看人的方式。

branches.en: THE PRACTICE AND ITS PURSE: making portraits, and the commissions that pay for them.
branches.cn: 实践及其钱袋：制作肖像，以及为此付费的委托。

branches.en: MANY AND ONE: the collective body, then the older countable single picture.
branches.cn: 多与一：作品总称，然后是较早的可数单幅用法。

branches.en: IN WORDS: the practice borrowed for literary character-building.
branches.cn: 文字之中：这门实践被借去构建文学人物。

branches.en: GENRE AND MANNER: the category, then a distinctive way of working inside it.
branches.cn: 门类与手法：先是类别，再是类别内独特的工作方式。

branches.en: THE CAMERA: the same practice in a new medium.
branches.cn: 相机：同一实践在新媒介中的形态。

intro.en: Portraiture is a French noun of action and result; its ending is no longer productive in English, but the root family still is.
intro.cn: portraiture 是法语的动作与结果名词；其词尾在英语中已不再能产，但词根词族仍能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin protrahere and trahere are the deep sources; French supplied the -ure noun shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 protrahere 与 trahere 是深层来源；法语提供 -ure 的名词形态。

items.example: The prefix adds the sense of drawing out.
items.exampleCN: 前缀加上「拉出」之义。

items.example: The root also gives trace and tractor.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根还给出 trace 与 tractor。

items.example: The verb became English portray.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词成为英语 portray。

items.example: Literature and furniture use the same ending.
items.exampleCN: literature 与 furniture 用同一个词尾。

items.example: Portraiture filled the long gallery.
items.exampleCN: 肖像画挂满了长厅。

items.structure: French past participle used as noun
items.example: The portrait is signed on the back.
items.exampleCN: 这幅肖像在背面签名。

items.example: The portraitist preferred chalk.
items.exampleCN: 这位肖像画家偏爱粉笔。

items.example: The mural portrays the harvest.
items.exampleCN: 壁画描绘收获。

items.example: Self-portraiture runs through his late work.
items.exampleCN: 自我肖像贯穿他晚期的作品。

latinEntries.structure: Latin noun suffix of action or result

definition_zh: 风景画；风景绘画；（作为门类的）风景画艺术
definition_en: the genre of painting that depicts natural scenery, or a painting of this kind
core_image: 一片山谷被框进画布，远处退成淡蓝，近处的树留住了光
scene: 展厅入口的说明牌写着，这一整间都属于低地国家的风景画。The room is devoted to landscape painting from the Low Countries.
sceneCN: 这里 landscape painting 指「描绘自然景色的绘画门类」（第 1 个义项：以风景为题材的画类）；句意为这个展厅专门陈列低地国家的风景画。

pos.zh: 风景画（门类，不可数；可数时指一幅作品）

collocations.phrase: a landscape painting of the vale
collocations.zh: 一幅描绘山谷的风景画

derivatives.zh: landscape painting + -er（人）→ 风景画家；从「门类」转到「从业者」
sea + -scape + painting → 海景画；从「陆地」转到「海洋」题材
city + -scape + painting → 城市风景画；从「陆地」转到「城市」题材

senses.title: The genre of scenery painting
senses.titleCN: 以自然景色为题材的绘画门类
senses.definition: the genre of painting whose subject is natural or rural scenery
senses.definitionCN: 以自然或乡野景色为题材的绘画门类
senses.example: The room is devoted to landscape painting from the Low Countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个展厅专门陈列低地国家的风景画。
senses.why: The phrase joins the subject (landscape) to the medium (painting), so the genre is named by what it shows and how it is made.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把题材（landscape）与媒介（painting）连接起来，因此门类由「画什么」与「怎么画」共同命名。

senses.title: A particular landscape painting
senses.definition: one painting whose subject is scenery
senses.definitionCN: 以景色为题材的一幅画
senses.example: The landscape painting above the desk shows a flooded meadow.
senses.exampleCN: 书桌上方的风景画描绘一片被水淹的草地。
senses.why: Genre names are regularly used countably for their members, so one canvas can be called a landscape painting.
senses.whyCN: 门类名称常被可数地用于其成员，因此一幅画布可以被称为 a landscape painting。

senses.title: The activity of painting scenery
senses.definition: the activity or practice of painting landscapes
senses.definitionCN: 绘制风景的活动或实践
senses.example: Landscape painting took him outdoors in every season.
senses.exampleCN: 风景写生让他在每个季节都到户外去。
senses.why: The -ing noun also names the doing, and the compound inherits that double reading from painting.
senses.whyCN: -ing 名词也命名做的过程，复合词从 painting 继承了这种双重读法。

senses.title: A regional school or tradition
senses.definition: a recognised school or national tradition of scenery painting
senses.definitionCN: 受认可的风景画派或民族传统
senses.example: Dutch landscape painting invented the low horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 荷兰风景画发明了低地平线。
senses.why: A group of painters in one place develops shared conventions, so the phrase can name a school rather than a single work.
senses.whyCN: 一地的一群画家发展出共同惯例，因此这个短语可以命名一个画派，而非单件作品。

senses.title: A style of depicting land
senses.definition: a manner of depicting land, such as idealised, topographic or expressive
senses.definitionCN: 描绘土地的方式，如理想化、地形写实或表现性
senses.example: Topographical landscape painting recorded estates for their owners.
senses.exampleCN: 地形写实的风景画为地主记录产业。
senses.why: The same genre can serve different purposes, so the phrase also names an approach to the land rather than the category itself.
senses.whyCN: 同一门类可以服务不同目的，因此这个短语也命名对待土地的一种方式，而非类别本身。

senses.title: An academic subject
senses.definition: the subject as taught in art schools and universities
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术学校与大学中教授的科目
senses.example: Landscape painting is taught in the second year.
senses.exampleCN: 风景画在第二年教授。
senses.why: When a genre enters a curriculum, its name becomes a course title, a familiar institutional shift.
senses.whyCN: 当门类进入课程，其名称就成为课程名，这是常见的机构化转移。

senses.title: A market and collecting category
senses.definition: the grouping used by dealers and auction houses for scenery pictures
senses.definitionCN: 画商与拍卖行用于风景画的分类
senses.example: Landscape painting outsold portraiture that season.
senses.exampleCN: 那个季度风景画的销量超过肖像画。
senses.why: Markets sort pictures by subject because buyers collect by subject, so the genre name becomes a sales category.
senses.whyCN: 市场按题材分类，因为买家按题材收藏，因此门类名称成为销售类别。

senses.title: A category in exhibitions and prizes
senses.definition: a competition or exhibition division for scenery pictures
senses.definitionCN: 展览或比赛中的风景画分组
senses.example: The salon added a landscape painting prize in that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年沙龙增设了风景画奖。
senses.why: Juries need divisions, so a genre becomes an award category and the phrase acquires a competitive sense.
senses.whyCN: 评审需要分组，因此门类变成奖项类别，这个短语获得了竞赛义。

intro.en: Landscape painting joins landscape, a Dutch-derived art term of about 1600, to painting, the noun from Latin pingere. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: landscape painting 把约 1600 年来自荷兰语的艺术术语 landscape 与来自拉丁 pingere 的名词 painting 结合。年代均为约数。

items.en: Land meant 'ground, soil, a definite portion of the earth'; its deeper Indo-European origin is uncertain, and some scholars suspect a substratum word.
items.cn: land 意为「土地、土壤、地球上的一块区域」；其更早印欧来源不确定，一些学者怀疑是底层语言词。

items.en: The -scape ending comes from -ship, 'condition, state', through Middle Dutch -scap, as in landschap.
items.cn: -scape 词尾来自 -ship「状态、性质」，经中古荷兰语 -scap，如 landschap。

items.en: Dutch landschap named a region and, in painting, a view of scenery; it was a painters' term distinguishing scenery from the main subject.
items.cn: 荷兰语 landschap 指一个地区，在绘画中指景色；它是画家的术语，用来把景色与主体区分开。

items.en: English landscape is recorded about 1600 for 'a painting representing an extensive view of rural scenery'.
items.cn: 英语 landscape 约 1600 年有记录，指「表现广阔乡野景色的绘画」。

items.en: As Dutch pictures entered English collections, landscape became the name of a genre, and landscape painting named the practice.
items.cn: 随着荷兰画进入英国收藏，landscape 成为一个门类的名称，landscape painting 则命名这门实践。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): no single first citation for the compound is agreed; it spread with museum catalogues and art teaching in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个复合词没有公认的最早书证；它随 18 与 19 世纪的博物馆图录与艺术教育而普及。

note.en: Group one separates landscape painting from the shorter term and from its painter; group two separates it from genres that also depict land or water but for another purpose.
note.cn: 第一组把 landscape painting 与较短的术语及指人的形式分开；第二组把它与同样描绘土地或水域、但目的不同的门类分开。

entries.definition: The scenery itself, a view, or a picture of it; landscape painting specifies the painted genre.
entries.definitionCN: 景色本身、一片视野，或其图像；landscape painting 限定为绘画门类。

entries.definition: An artist who paints landscapes; the phrase names a maker, not a genre.
entries.definitionCN: 画风景的艺术家；这个短语指创作者，而非门类。

entries.definition: A picture or view dominated by the sea; it is a parallel formation with a different subject.
entries.definitionCN: 以海为主的图画或视野；是题材不同的平行构词。

entries.definition: A picture or view of a city; landscape painting usually implies rural or natural scenery.
entries.definitionCN: 城市的图画或视野；landscape painting 通常指乡野或自然景色。

entries.definition: A painting of a specific known view, often made for travellers; landscape painting can be idealised or generic.
entries.definitionCN: 描绘特定知名景色的画，常为旅行者而作；landscape painting 可以是理想化或泛化的。

entries.definition: Painting that records the precise features of a place; it is a documentary branch of landscape painting.
entries.definitionCN: 精确记录某地特征的绘画；是风景画中的纪实分支。

entries.definition: Painting of ordinary people's activities; it shares a low subject with landscape but centres on figures.
entries.definitionCN: 描绘普通人日常活动的画；与风景画同属较低题材，但以人物为中心。

entries.definition: The visible features of a landscape, or stage decoration; it is the subject, not the painting.
entries.definitionCN: 风景的可见特征，或舞台布景；是题材，不是绘画。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: land + -scape + painting: a painted view of land.
normal.cn: land + -scape + painting：画下来的土地景象。

normal.en: The term landscape came from Dutch landschap around 1600 as a painters' word.
normal.cn: landscape 约 1600 年作为画家用语来自荷兰语 landschap。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the genre: Dutch landscape painting, topographical landscape painting, a landscape painting prize.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出门类：荷兰风景画、地形写实风景画、风景画奖。

normal.en: The family runs landscape, landscape painter, seascape and cityscape.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 landscape、landscape painter、seascape 与 cityscape。

normal.en: The -scape ending is the old -ship, so a landscape is literally a 'land condition'.
normal.cn: -scape 词尾就是旧的 -ship，因此 landscape 字面是「土地的状态」。

abstract.en: Picture a valley folded into a rectangle and made to fit.
abstract.cn: 想象一片山谷被折进一个矩形并刚好合适。

abstract.en: Picture distance turning pale blue simply because it is far away.
abstract.cn: 想象远处仅因为远而变成淡蓝。

abstract.en: Picture a window that can be sold, stored and hung on another wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇可以出售、收藏并挂到另一面墙上的窗。

examples.en: Landscape painting rose when travel made distant views desirable.
examples.cn: 当旅行让远方景色变得可欲，风景画随之兴起。

examples.en: The collection pairs landscape painting with botanical drawing.
examples.cn: 这批收藏把风景画与植物素描配对陈列。

examples.en: She wrote on landscape painting as a form of national self-description.
examples.cn: 她研究风景画作为一种民族自我描述的形式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「land（土地）+ scape（景象）+ painting（画）」——画土地的景象 → 风景画

root: land 来自古英语 land「土地」，更早印欧来源不确定；-scape 来自 -ship「状态」，经中古荷兰语 -scap；landscape 约 1600 年指风景画。painting 来自拉丁 pingere。复合词 landscape painting 的首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the genre to one work, the activity, a school, a style, a course, a market category and an exhibition division.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从门类转到单幅作品、活动、画派、风格、课程、市场类别与展览分组。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a valley is framed onto canvas, the distance fading to pale blue and the near trees holding the light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片山谷被框进画布，远处退成淡蓝，近处的树留住了光。

branches.en: THE GENRE AND THE COURSE: the category, then the same name in a curriculum.
branches.cn: 门类与课程：类别，然后是课表中的同一名称。

branches.en: ONE WORK AND THE ACT: a single canvas, then the doing that made it.
branches.cn: 单件与行为：一幅画布，然后是制作它的行动。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: shared conventions in one place and time.
branches.cn: 画派：一地一时的共同惯例。

branches.en: THE APPROACH: idealised, topographic or expressive ways of seeing land.
branches.cn: 路径：理想化、地形写实或表现性地看待土地。

branches.en: THE MARKET AND THE PRIZE: subject-based selling, then subject-based judging.
branches.cn: 市场与奖项：按题材售卖，再按题材评审。

intro.en: The phrase has three parts: a Germanic land, a Germanic suffix worn down from -ship, and a Latin-derived painting.
intro.cn: 这个短语有三部分：日耳曼语的 land、由 -ship 磨损而来的日耳曼语词尾，以及拉丁来源的 painting。

latinIntro.en: Only painting has a Latin ancestor, pingere; landscape is Germanic through Dutch, and land's earlier origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 painting 有拉丁祖先 pingere；landscape 经荷兰语属日耳曼语，land 的更早来源不确定。

items.example: The land rises behind the house.
items.exampleCN: 房子后面的土地升高。

items.meaningCN: 状态或一片展开的景象
items.example: Seascape and cityscape use the same ending.
items.exampleCN: seascape 与 cityscape 用同一个词尾。

items.meaning: a region; a view; a picture of scenery
items.example: The landscape was painted from the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 这片景色是从山脊上画下的。

items.structure: Old French peindre, from Latin pingere
items.example: They painted the valley in oil.
items.exampleCN: 他们用油画描绘山谷。

items.example: Painting names both act and product.
items.exampleCN: painting 同时命名行为与产物。

items.example: The painting is unsigned.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画没有签名。

items.example: Landscape painting filled the west wall.
items.exampleCN: 风景画挂满了西墙。

items.example: The landscape painter worked on site.
items.exampleCN: 这位风景画家在现场作画。

items.example: The seascape hangs beside the landscape.
items.exampleCN: 海景画挂在风景画旁边。
